title: Matt Kindt Launches New Anthology 'Flux House Presents' This October
content:
Matt Kindt is back with a new project, and it looks fascinating. His highly anticipated anthology, 'Flux House Presents #1', hits shelves this October from Oni Press. Kindt, celebrated for his mind-bending thrillers like Mind MGMT and Dept. H, isn't flying solo. He's gathered a stellar lineup for this inaugural issue, featuring Ella Kindt, long-time collaborator Brian Hurtt, and David Lapham.

The "Flux House" moniker itself hints at something more than a typical anthology. Is this the genesis of a new creative collective or an imprint? Oni Press, a publisher renowned for championing creator-owned comics, is the perfect home. This series promises innovative storytelling from one of indie comics' most singular voices. Get ready.
excerpt: Matt Kindt, creator of Mind MGMT, is launching a new anthology series, 'Flux House Presents #1', this October via Oni Press. He's joined by Ella Kindt, Brian Hurtt, and David Lapham for what could be the start of a new creative collective.
imageAlt: Cover art for Flux House Presents #1 featuring an abstract, colorful design
pullQuote: The "Flux House" moniker itself hints at something more than a typical anthology.
editorNote: This could signal a major new creative hub for Matt Kindt, beyond just a single series. Fans of his intricate, layered storytelling should keep a close eye on "Flux House." It's exciting to see Oni Press continuing to back unique creator-owned visions like this.

title: Sabrina The Teenage Witch Conjures New Ongoing Series for October 2026
content:
Get ready to feel the hex! Oni Press is conjuring up some serious magic, giving us a first look inside Sabrina The Teenage Witch #1, a brand-new ongoing series slated for an October 2026 launch. This isn't just another reboot; it's a bold new chapter for an iconic character, helmed by an award-winning creative team.

Hugo Award-nominated writer Corinna Bechko, known for her gripping work on Green Lantern: Earth One, is teaming up with Eisner Award-nominated artist Kano, whose dynamic art has graced titles like Daredevil. Together, they're set to redefine Sabrina Spellman for a new generation of readers. Nick Cagnetti also contributes additional art, crafting a special guide to familiars that promises extra lore.

The series dives straight in with Sabrina grappling with a newly revealed secret birthright. She's balancing the crushing realities of being a 16-year-old high schooler with mastering her burgeoning magical powers. It's a classic teen struggle, but this time, it comes with a Halloween backdrop, amplifying the spooky vibes in Greendale.

Things quickly go sideways when Sabrina's notoriously sarcastic feline familiar, Salem, accidentally unleashes a mythical trickster. This forces Sabrina's two worlds – the mundane and the magical – into a spectacular collision. No time for homework, just pure supernatural chaos! Fans have been yearning for a fresh, substantive take on the character, and Bechko and Kano seem ready to deliver a truly magical experience.

This new Sabrina series leads Oni Press's October 2026 solicitations. The lineup also includes Archie #2, continuing the main Riverdale narrative with Ben H. Winters and Fábio Moon. Additionally, Oni is re-releasing acclaimed compact editions of previous Sabrina runs by Kelly Thompson and Veronica Fish, alongside Chip Zdarsky and Erica Henderson's fan-favorite Jughead series. It's clear Archie Comics is not just looking forward but also celebrating its rich, diverse legacy.
excerpt: Oni Press is launching a new Sabrina The Teenage Witch ongoing series in October 2026, featuring Hugo Award-nominated writer Corinna Bechko and Eisner Award-nominated artist Kano. Fans get a first look inside as Sabrina balances high school life and newly revealed magical powers, all while dealing with a mythical trickster unleashed by Salem.
imageAlt: Key art for Sabrina The Teenage Witch #1 showing Sabrina Spellman with her cat Salem, against a magical backdrop.
pullQuote: Bechko and Kano seem ready to deliver a truly magical experience for Sabrina fans.
editorNote: This new series is a huge deal for Sabrina fans, especially with such acclaimed talent at the helm. It's exciting to see Oni Press invest in a character with such a rich, albeit often-reinvented, history. Keep an eye on how this new iteration connects to the broader Archie-verse.

KPop Demon Hunters continues its impressive expansion into global pop culture, leveraging the massive appeal of Squishmallows to reach new audiences. It highlights the growing trend of webtoons crossing over into diverse merchandise, proving their mainstream appeal beyond the digital page. Get ready to collect!

title: Sabrina's Back! Oni Press Conjures Up Major October 2026 Solicits
content:
Oni Press is gearing up for a monster October 2026, dropping a major new Sabrina the Teenage Witch series and a star-studded anthology. Get ready, Riverdale fans: Sabrina Spellman is back!

The biggest news? Sabrina the Teenage Witch #1 launches this October, helmed by Hugo Award-nominated writer Corinna Bechko and Eisner Award-nominated artist Kano. They're throwing the iconic sorceress-in-training into a brand-new ongoing series, just in time for Halloween. Sabrina’s got typical teenage woes, her secret magical heritage, and now a mythical trickster unleashed by her familiar, Salem. It sounds like pure Archie Comics mischief, but with a serious magical punch. This isn't just a reboot; it's a spectacular new era.

Also hitting shelves is Flux House Presents #1, a quarterly comics showcase led by New York Times bestselling writer and Eisner Award nominee Matt Kindt. Kindt, known for his mind-bending work on BRZRKR and Mind MGMT, brings in frequent collaborators Brian Hurtt and David Lapham. This 64-page anthology promises first appearances and thrilling introductions to new Flux House series. Expect wild, unpredictable storytelling from one of the medium's most acclaimed creators.

On the collected edition front, fans have waited years for this: the Afterlife with Archie Deluxe Edition HC. Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and Francesco Francavilla's genre-defining horror series, which famously unleashed a zombie apocalypse on Riverdale, finally gets its complete collection. This definitive hardcover includes the never-before-collected issues #6-10 and a full cover gallery. It’s a must-have for anyone who wants to revisit Archie’s darkest timeline.

Oni isn't stopping there. Jarrett Melendez and Irene Flores return with Chef's Kiss Again, the sequel to their Alex Award-winning queer romance graphic novel. Ben and Liam are back, navigating dream jobs, new responsibilities, and the anxieties of a blossoming relationship. For those seeking something truly unique, look for international graphic novels like Yoann Kavege's wordless, intergalactic odyssey Moon Deer and Mathieu Bablet's optimistic, climate-focused Silent Jenny, both translated from French. These are thoughtful, visually striking stories that push the boundaries of the medium.

While new series and deluxe editions grab headlines, fan-favorite series continue. Look for new issues of Archie, Fort Psycho, The Forever Home, and Cruel Kingdom. Meanwhile, Super Mondo Mega Mutts, Adventure Time: Quadruple Feature, Biker Mice from Mars: Scorch, and Faceless and the Family wrap up their runs. Oni Press is clearly committed to a diverse lineup, balancing beloved characters with fresh, globally sourced voices and ambitious creator-owned projects.
excerpt: Oni Press's October 2026 lineup drops a major new ongoing series, Sabrina the Teenage Witch #1, from writer Corinna Bechko and artist Kano. It also features Matt Kindt's new anthology Flux House Presents #1 and the long-awaited Afterlife with Archie Deluxe Edition. The publisher balances iconic characters with diverse creator-owned and international graphic novels.
imageAlt: Cover art for Sabrina the Teenage Witch #1 featuring Sabrina Spellman, Salem the cat, and other magical elements.
pullQuote: This isn't just a reboot; it's a spectacular new era.
editorNote: This fall looks strong for Oni Press, showing a clear strategy to blend big-name character launches with acclaimed creator-owned projects and diverse international titles. Fans of classic Archie characters will want to jump on Sabrina, but don't sleep on the innovative graphic novels pushing the medium forward. It's a smart play in a competitive market.

title: Erased Creator Kei Sanbe Dives Into Mystery Adventure with Aria's Adventures in Miracleland
content:
Kei Sanbe, the visionary behind the acclaimed psychological thriller Erased (Boku Dake ga Inai Machi), is embarking on a dramatic genre shift with his new manga, Aria's Adventures in Miracleland. Set to debut in the July 2026 issue of Young Ace, this new series promises a departure from the dark suspense fans have come to expect.

The story centers on Aria, a girl who struggles to fit in. Her life takes an unexpected turn when she awakens on a mysterious, seemingly uninhabited island. The premise hints at a blend of survival, self-discovery, and perhaps the signature Sanbe mystery that kept readers gripped in his past works.

Sanbe is renowned for crafting intricate narratives with high stakes and emotional depth. Erased, in particular, earned critical acclaim for its time-traveling murder mystery. This new venture into what sounds like a fantastical adventure raises questions: Will Sanbe infuse Miracleland with the same underlying tension? Or is this a fresh start, exploring themes of wonder and exploration more directly? Fans are eager to see how his storytelling prowess translates to this new canvas. It's a significant move for an author known for such a distinct style.
excerpt: Kei Sanbe, creator of the hit psychological thriller Erased, is launching a brand new manga titled Aria's Adventures in Miracleland. The series follows an outcast girl, Aria, who wakes up on a mysterious island, marking a potential genre shift for Sanbe into adventure and fantasy.
imageAlt: Cover art for Kei Sanbe's new manga, Aria's Adventures in Miracleland, featuring a young girl on a mysterious island
pullQuote: This new series promises a departure from the dark suspense fans have come to expect.
editorNote: This is huge news! Sanbe moving from psychological thrillers to something more fantastical is an exciting prospect. Fans will want to watch for hints of his signature suspense woven into Aria's journey. It's a bold move, and we're here for it.

title: The 7 Day: Reading Friday's Manga & Anime News Through the Number of Inquiry
content:
Today's Number: 7

On Friday, July 17, 2026, the day's headlines arrive under the sign of the 7 — the numerologist's number of inquiry, a vibration of analysis, secrecy, and the search for truth. It is a useful lens, if only a literary one, for reading a news cycle led this morning by "Trump Demands Network Licenses Revoked: Accuses ABC, NBC of Treating Him Like Past Presidents." Strip away the mysticism and the number still works as a mood: the stories crossing the wire share a common temperature, and today that temperature reads as inquiry.

Set "Trump Demands Network Licenses Revoked: Accuses ABC, NBC of Treating Him Like Past Presidents" beside "Jujutsu Kaisen Season 3: Culling Game Heats Up with Major Showdowns!" and a thread begins to show. The two stories come from different desks — perhaps different corners of the industry — yet both turn on the same underlying tension that the 7 tends to surface: the pull between what is being started and what is being held together. Read together rather than apart, the day's lead items stop looking like isolated announcements and start looking like a single weather system.

The Connective Thread

Beneath the lead, the supporting stories — "Hans Zimmer's Hidden Gem: Wallace & Gromit Soundtrack Hits Vinyl", "Uma Musume Rides West: LA to Host World Tour Concert with 17-Member Cast", "Arakure Unsheathes Vengeance in For Honor's New Season", "Kevin Knight Crashes Kenny Omega's World Title Celebration, All In Hype Builds" — fill in the pattern. Coverage from Bleeding Cool and Anime News Network keeps circling the same themes: franchises under strain, decisions deferred, and the quiet recalculation of who holds the initiative. None of these stories was written with the others in mind, which is precisely why their convergence is worth noting. The job of analysis is to read the cycle as a whole, and the whole, today, leans hard into inquiry.

Catzye scanned 40 headlines across the major manga and anime feeds today. Of those, 2 carry titles that reduce, letter by letter, to today's number 7. That is a coincidence of language rather than fate — but it is the kind of coincidence that makes you look twice, and looking twice is the whole point of reading the news slowly.

Among those number-7 headlines: "Hellraiser Revival Dev Diary Unveils New Vision of Hell"; "Zoe Saldaña, Nicole Kidman's Lioness Season 3 Trailer Unleashed". Whatever you make of the arithmetic, the stories themselves reward attention. Each one, in its way, is a story about analysis, secrecy, and the search for truth — which is to say, a story about the choices facing the people in it.

What To Watch

If the 7 is the number of inquiry, then the test of the next few days is whether today's openings are followed through or quietly abandoned. Numerology would call that the difference between the number's higher and lower expression. A journalist would just call it the follow-up — the second-day story that tells you whether the first one mattered. Either way, the questions are the same: who acts, who waits, and who pays for the delay.

Catzye's daily analysis reads the news through the lens of the day's number. It is not a forecast. It is a way of paying attention — a reminder that the headlines, however scattered, tend to rhyme. Check back tomorrow, when the number turns over and the pattern shifts with it.

A Note on Method

Every headline on this page was pulled from our newsroom feeds and reduced using standard Pythagorean numerology — each letter mapped to a digit one through nine, summed by word, then reduced until a single digit or master number remains. The same arithmetic that gives a name its Destiny number gives a headline its vibration. We make no claim that the universe arranges the news to suit a number. We claim only that a constraint, even an arbitrary one, is a good way to force fresh attention onto stories you might otherwise scroll past — and that the day's events, read together, almost always tell a more coherent story than any one of them does alone.

title: Trump Demands Network Licenses Revoked: Accuses ABC, NBC of Treating Him Like Past Presidents
content:
Alright, buckle up. While we're usually knee-deep in seasonal anime rankings and manga release dates, something truly wild just hit the mainstream news. Former President Donald Trump recently called for ABC and NBC to have their broadcast licenses revoked. His grievance? The networks apparently committed the grave sin of treating his latest public address like they'd treat speeches from Presidents Obama and Biden – by choosing not to air it.

Trump, never one to mince words (or avoid a dramatic flair), accused the networks of "continuing this fraud" and working to "protect the radical left." He argued they use public airwaves for free and, therefore, owe the public "honesty in elections and reporting." He even signaled to FCC Commissioner Brendan Carr for action.

However, anyone familiar with network TV knows this isn't some unprecedented slight. Networks have a track record of passing on presidential addresses if they deem them more political than a matter of national importance. It happened in 2022 when ABC aired a game show over a Biden speech, and back in 2014 with an Obama immigration address. Given the predictable outcome of Trump's latest teleprompter adventure, it seems ABC and NBC probably made the right call. Maybe they should have just re-aired an old Gundam series; at least that has consistent lore.
excerpt: Former President Donald Trump is demanding ABC and NBC have their broadcast licenses revoked. His reason? They chose not to air his recent address, treating it similarly to how they've handled speeches from past presidents like Obama and Biden. This isn't an isolated incident, as networks have a history of prioritizing regular programming over political addresses.
imageAlt: Former President Donald Trump speaking at a podium with logos of ABC and NBC visible in the background
pullQuote: Trump's grievance? The networks apparently committed the grave sin of treating his latest public address like they'd treat speeches from Obama and Biden.
editorNote: This whole debacle really highlights the ongoing tension between political grandstanding and media responsibility. For fans, it's a stark reminder that even mainstream news can get caught up in drama that feels straight out of a poorly written political thriller. Maybe next time, the networks should just air a classic mecha anime instead; far less divisive.

title: Hans Zimmer's Hidden Gem: Wallace & Gromit Soundtrack Hits Vinyl
content:
Hold onto your hats, Aardman fans! The Oscar-winning soundtrack for Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit is finally getting a vinyl release, arriving September 18. But here's the real surprise: none other than Hans Zimmer produced the score. That's a serious pedigree for a beloved animated classic, putting it in rare company.

Julian Nott, the musical genius behind the iconic Wallace & Gromit theme since their very first short, composed the film's full score. Curse of the Were-Rabbit was a monumental achievement for Aardman, not only clinching an Academy Award for Best Animated Film but also marking their second feature-length masterpiece after the equally cherished Chicken Run. Nott's work on Were-Rabbit earned him an Annie Award and an International Film Music Critics Award, cementing his legacy with the inventive duo.

What's truly wild is the origin story of that instantly recognizable main theme. Nott once confessed he improvised the entire melody just hours before a recording session! It burst forth from a late-night session at the piano, born purely from his improvisatory spirit. Talk about last-minute brilliance shaping animation history.

Varèse Sarabande and Craft Recordings are bringing this cherished piece of animated magic to turntables. It's a must-have for any soundtrack collector or long-time fan of Wallace, Gromit, and their stop-motion adventures.
excerpt: The Oscar-winning soundtrack for Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit is hitting vinyl on September 18, and it comes with a surprising credit: Hans Zimmer as producer. Julian Nott, the franchise's longtime composer, masterfully scored the film, even improvising its iconic theme just hours before recording. This release is a treat for fans of Aardman's stop-motion magic.
imageAlt: Cover art for Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit vinyl soundtrack, featuring the duo.
pullQuote: Nott once confessed he improvised the entire melody just hours before a recording session!
editorNote: This release is more than just a soundtrack; it's a testament to the enduring charm and musical brilliance of Wallace & Gromit. Fans will love revisiting this Oscar-winning score, and discovering the surprising involvement of a legendary producer like Hans Zimmer adds an exciting layer to Aardman's history. Get ready to spin some cheese and chase some rabbits.

title: Uma Musume Rides West: LA to Host World Tour Concert with 17-Member Cast
content:
Uma Musume: Pretty Derby is officially riding global! The mega-popular multimedia franchise brings its 7th Event World Tour: The Stage to Los Angeles this October 22-23. This marks a rare overseas venture for Cygames' idolized horse girl juggernaut, a significant nod to its massive international fanbase.

Seventeen voice actors are confirmed to take the stage, a huge lineup promising dynamic live performances embodying their beloved characters. For years, these elaborate concerts were confined to Japan. Now, LA fans get their chance to experience the high-energy spectacle firsthand. This is a big step for Uma Musume, signaling its intent to expand its global footprint. It's a clear win for fans outside Japan.
excerpt: The global phenomenon Uma Musume: Pretty Derby is bringing its highly anticipated 7th Event World Tour, 'The Stage,' to Los Angeles on October 22-23. Seventeen voice actors are confirmed to perform live, marking a significant international expansion for the beloved franchise.

title: Arakure Unsheathes Vengeance in For Honor's New Season
content:
Ubisoft is unleashing Arakure, a new Samurai assassin, into For Honor on July 23 as part of Year 10 Season 2. This isn't just another fighter; Arakure arrives with a dark past and a burning vendetta. Born into crime, she seeks vengeance against the Samurai, whose Orochi guards killed her brother. She plans to desecrate the Khatun statue during the Samurai Feast, a bold statement against those she despises.

Gameplay-wise, Arakure is a quick-hitting striker, prioritizing agility and precise damage over brute force. She's designed for swift eliminations, not tanking hits.

Fans also get more than just a new hero. The popular Starter Dominion event returns from July 23 to August 6, bringing its skill-focused gameplay back – notably, without Gear Perks, but with Stamina, Feats, and Revenge now enabled. Plus, the Metal Trials throwback event and Hero Fests are making a comeback.
excerpt: For Honor welcomes Arakure, a new Samurai assassin, on July 23 with a story of vengeance and swift combat. This agile striker seeks to desecrate a Samurai statue in Year 10 Season 2, which also revives popular events like Starter Dominion.
imageAlt: Key art for For Honor featuring the new samurai assassin Arakure with her weapons
pullQuote: Born into crime, she seeks vengeance against the Samurai, whose Orochi guards killed her brother.
editorNote: Arakure's deep backstory is a welcome touch for a fighting game character, giving players more than just new moves to master. Fans will want to jump into the updated Starter Dominion too; playing without Gear Perks really shifts the meta. It's a great opportunity to test out Arakure's agility without relying on buffs.

title: Kevin Knight Crashes Kenny Omega's World Title Celebration, All In Hype Builds
content:
Kenny Omega's triumphant return as AEW World Champion hit an immediate snag, as TNT Champion Kevin Knight shockingly ambushed him during his celebration. Knight's bold move sets up an unexpected AEW World Championship match at AEW Redemption, throwing a wrench into Omega's path toward Will Ospreay at All In: London.

The Boston crowd was electric as Tony Schiavone hosted Omega's long-awaited celebration. The Young Bucks presented Omega with the proper AEW World Championship, allowing him to finally address the fans about his arduous journey back to the top. But as Omega soaked in the moment, Will Ospreay emerged, praising Omega before pivoting to their monumental clash at All In: London. This is the match fans have waited years for, and the build is palpable.

Then, the real twist: TNT Champion Kevin Knight interrupted, not to praise, but to challenge Omega for the AEW World Championship at Redemption. Omega accepted, but dared Knight to do it without Don Callis. Knight's chilling reply—“no goodness left in my heart, only greatness”—preceded a brutal microphone strike to Omega. This is a significant heel turn for Knight, clearly influenced by Callis, and a clear signal he’s no longer playing by the rules. The ensuing chaos saw Darby Allin and Brian Cage ignite a brawl, leading to Omega, Jon Moxley, Claudio Castagnoli, and Ospreay fending off the Don Callis Family in a wild scene.

Earlier, Jon Moxley had delivered pointed advice to Will Ospreay: when his shot at Omega comes, he must “pull the trigger.” This isn't just a friendly chat; it's a stark warning about the high stakes of their All In encounter. This match isn't just for a title; it's for legacy.

Mercedes Moné also made a hometown splash, teaming with AEW Women's World Tag Team Champions Divine Dominion to defeat Willow Nightingale, Maya World, and Hyan. Moné secured the pinfall with the Moné Maker, proving her status as a top contender and a fan favorite in Boston. Her presence continues to elevate the women's division.

Elsewhere, Andrade El Ídolo continued his crusade against the Don Callis Family. He defeated Jake Doyle, earning an AEW National Championship match against Mark Davis at Redemption. Intriguingly, Andrade revealed he possesses MJF's Dynamite Diamond Ring, heavily implying Will Ospreay's behind-the-scenes assistance. This adds another layer to the complex web of alliances and betrayals brewing around Callis.

The AEW World Tag Team Championship saw Christian Cage and Adam Copeland retain against Daniel Garcia and Wheeler Yuta, though not without controversial tactics. Post-match, a massive brawl erupted, highlighting the ever-present faction warfare across AEW's tag division.

Other notable developments include Kyle Fletcher defending the AEW International Championship in a chaotic match involving Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Bandido, and Brody King, setting up Fletcher vs. Bandido for Redemption. Darby Allin earned a TNT Championship match against Kevin Knight next week, setting up another high-stakes encounter. The Brawling Birds (Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor) also announced their return, with their sights set firmly on Wembley Stadium. Chris Jericho accepted Tommaso Ciampa's challenge for Redemption, promising a brutal encounter with the Painmaker.

AEW is clearly building towards a pivotal summer with Redemption and the monumental All In: London. The landscape is shifting rapidly, with champions under fire and new alliances forming.
excerpt: Kevin Knight unexpectedly crashed Kenny Omega's AEW World Championship celebration, challenging Omega for the title at AEW Redemption and creating immediate tension before Omega's highly anticipated All In clash with Will Ospreay. Mercedes Moné secured a significant hometown victory, while Andrade El Ídolo revealed a major connection to MJF's Dynamite Diamond Ring in his ongoing feud with the Don Callis Family. The episode set a dynamic stage for a summer of high-stakes championship matches and evolving rivalries.
imageAlt: Kenny Omega holding the AEW World Championship belt, looking surprised and holding his neck, with Kevin Knight in the background holding a microphone.
pullQuote: Kevin Knight shockingly ambushed Kenny Omega during his celebration, setting up an unexpected AEW World Championship match at Redemption.
editorNote: This is a classic pro-wrestling move, but Kevin Knight striking Omega with the mic was brutal and instantly established him as a major threat. What's interesting is how this affects the Omega vs. Ospreay narrative for All In; a grueling match at Redemption could definitely impact Omega's chances. Fans will want to watch how Don Callis continues to manipulate these championship pictures.

title: Insomniac's Wolverine Drops New Trailer, Skips Actual Gameplay (For Now)
content:
Insomniac Games just dropped a new trailer for Marvel's Wolverine, and while it's packed with Logan's signature anti-hero grit, there's a crucial catch: this isn't actual in-game footage. Instead, it's a cinematic montage showing Wolverine's brutal, battle-scarred journey across different eras and teams. It's a hype reel, not a gameplay reveal.

The anticipation for Insomniac's take on Wolverine has been sky-high since its announcement. This trailer doubles down on the dark, emotionally charged narrative hinted at previously. Logan, seemingly done with his berserker ways, is pulled back into the fray with Team X. Their mission? Stop Bolivar Trask, who's kidnapping mutants. This global fight takes Wolverine from the frosted Canadian Wilderness to the bustling streets of Tokyo and the shadowy Marvel island nation of Madripoor.

Players can expect razor-sharp adamantium claw combat, fluid attacks, and the ability to customize Wolverine's fighting style with unique Techniques and Adaptations. Face off against classic villains like Omega Red and Trask's Reavers. Beneath the explosive brutality, the game promises to delve deep into Wolverine's forgotten past, exploring themes of identity, loyalty, and his perpetual struggle. Fans have waited years for a definitive Wolverine experience, and Insomniac looks ready to deliver.
excerpt: Insomniac Games released a new cinematic trailer for Marvel's Wolverine, showcasing Logan's anti-hero journey across time and conflicts. While visually striking, the trailer notably features pre-rendered clips, not actual in-game footage. Fans can still glimpse the dark, emotionally charged story and brutal combat promised for the highly anticipated title.
imageAlt: Cinematic shot of Wolverine in his classic costume, claws extended, from the new game trailer.
pullQuote: It's not just about tearing through foes; it's about the man beneath the claws.
editorNote: This trailer continues to build intense hype for Insomniac's Wolverine, even without showing gameplay. It reinforces the mature, character-driven tone fans have been craving. Now, the real wait begins for that first glimpse of how this beast actually plays.

title: Star Trek: Voyager Game Unveils Expansion Pass, Adds USS Equinox
content:
Star Trek: Voyager – Across The Unknown just dropped a bombshell: an Expansion Pass is coming, and it promises to bring the infamous USS Equinox into play. Developer Gamexcite and publisher Daedalic Entertainment are clearly listening to fans, adding content many felt was missing from the base game.

First up is the "Delta Chronicles" DLC, available now. It packs five new side missions, drawing directly from iconic Voyager episodes like "The Omega Directive" and "Distant Origin." What's cool is that players can make their own choices, potentially altering outcomes from the show. Plus, you can now recruit holographic Reginald Barclay and the Voth scientist Dr. Gegen as playable heroes. Four new NPC ships, including the formidable Voth City Ship and a recruitable Ferengi Marauder, spice up the Delta Quadrant. New tech also rounds out the package.

Alongside the premium DLC, a free Patch 1.8 hit today. It’s a solid update, adding seven new ship quests, UI upgrades, balancing tweaks, and quality-of-life improvements. This patch clearly comes from community feedback, which is always great to see.

The Expansion Pass itself will roll out four premium DLCs over the next year. Future content includes more side missions and, crucially, the USS Equinox as a playable starship for an upcoming game mode. A new sector based on another celebrated Voyager episode is also on the way. These additions promise to offer entirely new ways to explore the Delta Quadrant, making a fresh playthrough appealing even for veteran captains.
excerpt: Star Trek: Voyager – Across The Unknown announced a new Expansion Pass, with the first DLC, "Delta Chronicles," available now. Fans can look forward to new side missions based on iconic episodes, playable characters like holographic Reginald Barclay, and the infamous USS Equinox joining the game as a playable starship in a future update.
imageAlt: Key visual for Star Trek: Voyager – Across The Unknown featuring the USS Voyager in the Delta Quadrant, with new characters and ships.
entities: Star Trek: Voyager – Across The Unknown
pullQuote: The Expansion Pass promises to bring the infamous USS Equinox into play, a move many fans will celebrate.
editorNote: This is a big win for Voyager fans who felt some classic elements were missing from the base game. The inclusion of the Equinox as a playable ship is a smart move, tapping into a memorable, darker chapter of Voyager's journey. It'll be interesting to see how these branching narrative choices play out and if they pave the way for more 'what if' scenarios in future Star Trek games.

title: Mad Cave Unleashes Dave Johnson's Pop Kill Variants for SDCC Exclusives
content: Mad Cave Studios is bringing serious firepower to San Diego Comic-Con. They just announced a slate of convention-exclusive variants, but the main event? Legendary artist Dave Johnson's 'Nice' and 'Naughty' covers for Pop Kill #1. Johnson, known for his impactful style on books like 100 Bullets, commands a huge following. His limited-edition work often vanishes fast. These Pop Kill variants are guaranteed collector magnets, especially with their 'Black Bag' exclusive status. Mad Cave clearly wants to own the con buzz this year.
excerpt: Mad Cave Studios is set to drop an impressive lineup of convention-exclusive variants at San Diego Comic-Con. The biggest draw? Legendary artist Dave Johnson's stunning 'Nice' and 'Naughty' covers for Pop Kill #1, which are already generating major collector buzz.

editorNote: This move from Mad Cave signals a clear intent to capture collector buzz at SDCC. Pairing a hot new title like Pop Kill with a veteran artist like Dave Johnson is a smart play. Fans should move fast, as these variants will undoubtedly sell out quickly at the con.

title: Kratos Actor Ryan Hurst Reportedly Injured, God of War Production Potentially Delayed to 2027
content:
The highly anticipated live-action God of War series on Amazon has hit a major snag: lead actor Ryan Hurst, cast as Kratos, reportedly suffered a bicep injury during a stunt, potentially pushing production as far back as 2027. This is a massive blow for fans eager to see the iconic PlayStation saga brought to life.

According to TMZ, Hurst tore his bicep and requires surgery. While production initially hoped for a mid-August return, the recovery timeline makes that impossible. Amazon Studios, alongside Sony Pictures TV, declined to comment on the report, but the prospect of a multi-year delay casts a long shadow over the adaptation.

Ronald D. Moore (Battlestar Galactica) helms the series as showrunner. He previously confirmed Amazon had greenlit two seasons, underscoring their commitment to this daunting property. The series aims to follow the critically acclaimed 2018 game, focusing on Kratos and Atreus's poignant journey to spread Faye's ashes. Callum Vinson plays Atreus, with a strong supporting cast including Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Frederick E.O. Toye (Shogun) is set to direct the first two episodes.

A potential 2027 restart is an eternity in TV production. Fans will undoubtedly feel this delay, especially after waiting years for a faithful adaptation. Hopefully, Hurst makes a full recovery, and production can resume sooner than anticipated.
excerpt: The highly anticipated live-action God of War series on Amazon faces a major setback after lead actor Ryan Hurst (Kratos) reportedly suffered a bicep injury during a stunt. This unexpected delay could push production for the two-season greenlit series as far back as 2027, leaving fans in limbo.
imageAlt: Ryan Hurst as Kratos and Callum Vinson as Atreus in a promotional image for the God of War live-action series.
pullQuote: A bicep injury for Kratos actor Ryan Hurst reportedly halts God of War production, potentially pushing its return to 2027.
editorNote: This is a huge setback for a series that already carries immense pressure from a devoted fanbase. A multi-year delay at this stage is almost unheard of for such a high-profile adaptation. Fans will want to watch closely for official confirmation and any revised timelines.

title: Chainsmoker Cat's Yani Unleashes 'Felony-Grade' Farts in Wild Debut
content:
Chainsmoker Cat isn't pulling any punches, and frankly, some viewers might need a hazmat suit. The new short-form anime, now streaming its first three episodes, has immediately polarized audiences with its relentless, no-holds-barred approach to comedy. Forget subtle gags; this series goes straight for the gut—literally.

The standout (or stand-out offensive) character, Yani, is quickly becoming infamous. Their "wretched farts" aren't just a running joke; our reviewer noted they "should be registered as felony-grade weapons of chemical warfare." That's the level of absurdity and gross-out humor we're talking about. The show's creators seem dedicated to pushing boundaries, clearly "committed to earning their godforsaken yuks," as our review snippet put it.

This isn't for everyone. Chainsmoker Cat feels like a deliberate challenge to conventional anime humor, perhaps aiming for a cult following among fans of irreverent, adult animation. It's crude, it's shocking, and it absolutely refuses to apologize. Whether that's genius or pure garbage will be up to individual viewers to decide, but one thing is certain: you won't forget Yani.
excerpt: The new short-form anime Chainsmoker Cat has instantly polarized audiences with its extreme, no-holds-barred comedy. Character Yani's 'wretched farts' are described as 'felony-grade weapons of chemical warfare,' signaling a deliberate push against conventional anime humor.
imageAlt: Chainsmoker Cat key visual featuring Yani the cat looking mischievous and surrounded by green gas
pullQuote: Yani's wretched farts should be registered as felony-grade weapons of chemical warfare.
editorNote: What's interesting here is the show's blatant disregard for subtlety, which could signal a growing trend in niche anime pushing extreme shock humor. Fans of crude adult animation will want to check this out, but be warned, it's not for the faint of heart.

title: Zelda Teams with Hasbro for New Toy Line, SDCC '26 Reveal Set
content: A legendary collaboration is brewing: Nintendo and Hasbro are teaming up for a new The Legend of Zelda toy line. This is huge news for fans who've craved more premium collectibles from the iconic franchise. The first look is set for San Diego Comic-Con in 2026. Hasbro's involvement suggests high-quality action figures or detailed collectibles are on the horizon. Get ready to add some Hyrule magic to your collection!
excerpt: Nintendo and Hasbro announced a new The Legend of Zelda toy collaboration, with the first reveal scheduled for San Diego Comic-Con in 2026. Fans have long awaited a significant push for premium collectibles from the beloved franchise.

title: The Overstreet Guide is Back — Here’s Why Your Manga Collection Needs It
content:
The definitive word on comic book condition is back. The Overstreet Guide to Grading Comics has returned, once again offering the gold standard for assessing a collectible's true worth. This isn't just about dusty comic shops; it’s a critical resource for anyone in the serious collecting game—yes, that includes manga fans.

Longtime industry expert Jeff "JC" Vaughn leads the charge, exploring the guide's history, current challenges, and its future relevance. In a market increasingly driven by online sales and speculation, understanding what constitutes a "near mint" versus a "fine" condition isn't just academic; it's financially vital.

While Overstreet traditionally focused on Western comics, its principles are universal. Manga collectors with rare first prints, limited edition art books, or vintage issues know that condition dictates value. Scratches, spine creases, or sun fading can drastically alter a volume's price. A standardized system helps cut through the noise, providing transparency and protecting both buyers and sellers. This guide serves as the essential benchmark for ensuring fair pricing and authenticating treasured pieces of manga history.
excerpt: The definitive guide to comic grading, The Overstreet Guide to Grading Comics, has returned, with insights from Jeff "JC" Vaughn. This essential resource offers invaluable standards for assessing condition and rarity, crucial for manga collectors looking to understand the true worth of their prized volumes.
imageAlt: Cover of The Overstreet Guide to Grading Comics
entities: The Overstreet Guide to Grading Comics
pullQuote: Understanding a collectible's true condition is the bedrock of its market value, whether it’s a Golden Age comic or a rare manga first print.
editorNote: This release is a timely reminder that serious collecting requires serious standards. For manga fans eyeing rare volumes or special editions, learning the ropes of grading can protect investments and deepen appreciation. It's not just about value; it's about preserving the art.

title: Morrigan Aensland Meets Vampirella in Unexpected Crossover Comic
content:
Hold onto your soul gems! A crossover nobody saw coming is hitting shelves this November: legendary horror icon Vampirella is officially squaring off against Capcom's iconic monster fighters in Vampirella Vs Darkstalkers. This new one-shot comic comes from Dynamite and Udon.

Industry veteran Tim Seeley (Hack/Slash, Nightwing) is helming this unexpected clash. Dynamite CEO Nick Barrucci confirms this project has been years in the making. Seeley, a self-proclaimed crossover enthusiast, is clearly having a blast. He describes the story as "sexy" and a "mashing it up with lots of teeth and skin" – fitting for a battle between two of pop culture's most alluring anti-heroines.

The plot sees Vampirella hunting a mysterious succubus. She crosses paths with Morrigan Aensland, the legendary demon princess from Makai. Both find themselves in a cat-and-mouse game across New York City, realizing their own monstrous similarities. But the real curveball? They're both being tracked by the notoriously unhinged monster hunter, Baby Bonnie Hood. Fans can also expect to see other Darkstalkers favorites like Felicia and Lilith hinted on various covers. This promises a monster mashup unlike any other.
excerpt: Capcom's Darkstalkers and horror icon Vampirella are officially crossing over in a new one-shot comic, Vampirella Vs Darkstalkers, due out this November. Industry veteran Tim Seeley is writing the unexpected clash, which sees Vampirella hunting a succubus and encountering Morrigan Aensland in New York City.
imageAlt: Comic cover for Vampirella Vs Darkstalkers, featuring Vampirella, Morrigan Aensland, and Baby Bonnie Hood
pullQuote: A crossover nobody saw coming is hitting shelves this November.
editorNote: Unexpected crossovers are always a blast, especially when they bring together such distinct horror and fantasy universes. What's interesting here is the one-shot format, allowing a focused, explosive story. Fans will want to watch if this opens the door for more Capcom game characters to jump into the comic world.

title: Wally West's Kid Flash Races Back, But Not Until 2026
content:
Hold onto your speed force, collectors! McFarlane Toys just unveiled a new DC Multiverse Kid Flash figure, but don't expect Wally West to race onto your shelves until July 2026. Yes, that's nearly two years away for a pre-order announcement. This long lead time is certainly a curious move, even for McFarlane's robust DC line.

The figure brings back the classic Wally West as Kid Flash, sporting his iconic red and yellow costume. Wally's journey from Barry Allen's sidekick to taking on The Flash mantle himself cemented his legendary status in the DC universe. This figure aims for a slightly more mature sculpt, fitting the broader DC Multiverse aesthetic while still capturing the youthful energy of the Silver Age speedster. It comes with alternate hands and speed force lightning effects, essential for any dynamic display.

While the wait will be excruciating for completionists, the classic Wally West is a must-have. He's listed at $27.99. Keep an eye out; Black Adam, Black Mask, Sinestro, and Brainiac are also set to join this upcoming wave.
excerpt: McFarlane Toys has announced a new DC Multiverse Kid Flash figure featuring the classic Wally West, but collectors will have an unusually long wait: the release isn't expected until July 2026. The figure, sporting his iconic red and yellow costume, aims for a mature sculpt with dynamic Speed Force effects.
imageAlt: McFarlane Toys DC Multiverse Kid Flash DC Classic figure in his red and yellow costume with speed force effects
pullQuote: A new McFarlane Toys Kid Flash figure is available for pre-order, but don't expect it until July 2026.
editorNote: A nearly two-year lead time for a pre-order is almost unheard of in collectibles. What does this mean for McFarlane's production schedule? Fans will definitely want to watch if this becomes a new trend for future waves, and what other deep cuts might get this early announcement treatment.

title: Robert Kirkman to Headline Image Comics at SDCC 2026
content:
San Diego Comic-Con 2026 just got its first big reveal: Robert Kirkman will headline Image Comics’ presence. Yes, the creator behind global hits like The Walking Dead and Invincible is taking center stage. This isn't just another panel; it's a spotlight on one of creator-owned comics' most influential voices.

Image Comics is a hub for independent vision, a spirit that resonates deeply with manga and anime fans who value unique storytelling. Kirkman’s work, known for its deep character dives and genre-bending narratives, has already proven its adaptability with successful TV series. His involvement hints at significant announcements and a deeper look into his creative process. Expect exclusive reveals and discussions that will likely shape the conversation for Western comics well into 2026.
excerpt: Robert Kirkman, the mind behind The Walking Dead and Invincible, is set to headline Image Comics’ presence at San Diego Comic-Con 2026. This spotlight promises deep dives into creator-owned storytelling and hints at major announcements from one of Western comics' most influential figures.

title: Dark Horse Drops Surprise Comic for Stage Tour, Confirmed for Switch 2
content:
Dark Horse Comics just pulled a fast one at San Diego Comic-Con, surprise-launching a brand new comic based on the upcoming rhythm game Stage Tour. The limited-edition title is a physical exclusive for SDCC attendees, instantly becoming a sought-after collectible.

The comic boasts an indie-darling creative team: Zoe Tunnell writes, Liana Kangas provides the art, Diana Sousa colors, and Tyler Smith letters. This is a solid lineup bringing the world of Stage Tour to life beyond the screen.

Stage Tour, a new music rhythm game from RedOctane Games, is confirmed for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and notably, the Nintendo Switch 2. Expanding game lore through comics is a smart move, giving fans a deeper dive into the world and its bandmates. Attendees can grab the comic free at both the Stage Tour and Dark Horse booths. They can also get hands-on with the game's closed alpha demo and new Kramer Guitar Controller at Booth #2834. This is a big push for a new IP.
excerpt: Dark Horse Comics surprised everyone at SDCC with a new comic tie-in for the upcoming rhythm game Stage Tour. This limited-edition collectible, featuring acclaimed creators Zoe Tunnell and Liana Kangas, expands the game's lore and is exclusively available for attendees. Stage Tour is also confirmed for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and the Nintendo Switch 2, making this an early look at a multi-platform IP.
imageAlt: Cover art for the Stage Tour comic, featuring vibrant characters in a band playing instruments with the game's logo.
pullQuote: Stage Tour is confirmed for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, PC, and notably, the Nintendo Switch 2.
editorNote: This is a smart play from RedOctane and Dark Horse. Launching a comic at SDCC for an unreleased game, especially one confirmed for the hotly anticipated Switch 2, is a great way to build buzz. Fans of rhythm games and comic tie-ins should definitely keep an eye on Stage Tour.

title: Chloe Fineman Closes SNL Chapter After Seven Seasons
content: Chloe Fineman, a standout talent celebrated for her spot-on impressions, announced her departure from Saturday Night Live after seven seasons. This news hits just ahead of SNL's 52nd season, marking a significant shift for the long-running comedy institution. Fineman joined as a featured player in the 2019-2020 season, just before the global pandemic. Yet, the unexpected "SNL @ Home" era proved a surprising launchpad, giving her a unique platform to showcase her incredible range of celebrity impressions. She quickly became a fan favorite. In a heartfelt social media post, Fineman expressed profound gratitude for her time, calling SNL the "greatest privilege" of her life. She praised the tireless work of the crew and writers, openly sharing the intense emotional rollercoaster of sketch comedy, from crushing disappointment to pure elation — even for a sketch about "lipstick for thicc dogs." It's a familiar journey for anyone deeply invested in creative work. Fineman feels it's the right time for her next chapter. While she'll miss her SNL family, her impact on the show's recent history is undeniable.
excerpt: Chloe Fineman, known for her incredible celebrity impressions, has announced her departure from Saturday Night Live after seven impactful seasons. Her exit ahead of SNL's 52nd season marks a notable change, with Fineman expressing deep gratitude for her time on the show as she looks to her next chapter.
imageAlt: Chloe Fineman posing for a promotional photo, likely for Saturday Night Live
pullQuote: Calling SNL the 'greatest privilege' of her life, Fineman feels it's the right time for her next chapter.
editorNote: This departure marks the end of an era for SNL, as Fineman brought a distinct energy and impressive talent for impressions that resonated with audiences. Fans will be eager to see where her unique comedic voice lands next, and what new projects she'll tackle. What's interesting here is how much an artist's personal investment shapes such a long-running creative project.

title: Ben 10 Comic Replaced By Art-Packed 'Creator Files' Special, Teases New Villain
content:
Instead of a new Ben 10 comic this October, fans get an unexpected treat: Dynamite Entertainment is releasing "The Ben 10: Creator Files." This special issue offers an unprecedented look behind the scenes of the popular comic series, promising exclusive first-looks and never-before-seen designs. The main Ben 10 series takes a brief pause, returning in November.

"The Ben 10: Creator Files" is a direct "thank you" to readers. It dives deep into the creation process, from writer Joe Casey's scripts to artist Robert Carey's initial sketches and finished artwork. Fans will see how colors by Ren Spiller and lettering by Taylor Esposito bring the pages to life.

The special isn't just a breakdown; it's a treasure trove. It features a new interview with writer Joe Casey and showcases Robert Carey's earliest character designs for the franchise. Many of these sketches have never been shown publicly. Even more exciting, the "Creator Files" teases upcoming storylines and debuts designs for the next classic Ben 10 villain. Plus, a gallery of variant cover pin-ups, some showing the artistic process itself.

This deep dive offers Ben 10 enthusiasts a unique glimpse into the creative minds of Man of Action and the team bringing the alien-powered hero to comic pages. Joe Casey will even sign a limited number of copies.
excerpt: Dynamite Entertainment is swapping October's regular Ben 10 comic for a special "Creator Files" issue. This behind-the-scenes book promises exclusive looks at unreleased art, early character designs, and even teases the next classic villain for the series. The main comic returns in November.
imageAlt: Cover art for The Ben 10: Creator Files comic book, showing Ben Tennyson and various alien forms with artistic sketches in the background.
pullQuote: The "Creator Files" teases upcoming storylines and debuts designs for the next classic Ben 10 villain.
editorNote: This is a fantastic way for Dynamite to engage the Ben 10 fanbase, offering a unique peek behind the creative curtain. Fans of comic art and franchise development will definitely want to grab a copy. It also builds anticipation for the main series' return in November, knowing what’s coming.

title: Marvel Comics Relocates to Burbank, Steve Wacker Named Editor-in-Chief
content:
A significant industry shake-up is underway as Marvel Comics prepares for a major move. The publisher will relocate its operations to Burbank, California, signaling a deeper integration with parent company Disney. This geographical shift aims to align the comic arm more closely with Disney’s vast multimedia empire, potentially streamlining cross-platform storytelling across comics, film, and television.

Adding to these tectonic shifts, industry veteran Steve Wacker is stepping into the editor-in-chief role. Wacker brings a formidable track record, known for his impactful runs on titles like Amazing Spider-Man and Daredevil. His promotion suggests a renewed focus on creative direction and a fresh vision for Marvel's iconic lineup. Fans will be watching closely to see what these changes mean for the future of the Marvel universe, both on the page and on screen.
excerpt: Marvel Comics is making a major move, relocating its operations to Burbank, California, to align more closely with Disney. This geographical shift comes alongside a significant leadership change, as industry veteran Steve Wacker steps up to become the new editor-in-chief.
imageAlt: Marvel Comics logo against a backdrop of the Burbank skyline and Disney studio buildings.
pullQuote: Industry veteran Steve Wacker is taking the editor-in-chief reins, marking a significant leadership shift for the publisher.
editorNote: This move hints at even tighter integration between Marvel's comics and its massively successful film and TV divisions. Fans should brace for potential cross-media synergies and possibly a more unified editorial vision under Wacker's leadership. It's a big moment for the House of Ideas.

title: Mets Host Oscar-Winning 'KPOP Demon Hunters' Theme Night
content:
Oscar-winning animated feature "KPOP Demon Hunters" is hitting the baseball diamond. The New York Mets announced a special theme night on August 15th, celebrating the critically acclaimed film. It’s a bold crossover, bringing an Academy Award winner to a Major League Baseball stadium.

The film, known for snagging Best Animated Feature at the 98th Oscars, also saw its track "Golden" make history. Sung by EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami, "Golden" became the first K-pop song to win Best Original Song. That's a massive win for K-pop and animation on the global stage.

Fans attending the Mets game against the Washington Nationals can grab an exclusive KPop Demon Hunters Mets jersey. It’s part of a broader Korean Heritage Night celebration. This mashup signals a growing trend: major sports embracing popular anime and K-pop culture. It's not just a game; it's a cultural event.
excerpt: Oscar-winning animated feature "KPOP Demon Hunters" is getting a special theme night with the New York Mets on August 15th. The film, which won Best Animated Feature, also saw its K-pop song "Golden" make history by winning Best Original Song at the 98th Oscars. Fans can snag an exclusive jersey and celebrate Korean Heritage Night.
imageAlt: New York Mets KPop Demon Hunters theme night jersey with team logo and anime character
pullQuote: "Golden" became the first K-pop song to win Best Original Song, a massive win for K-pop and animation on the global stage.
editorNote: This crossover is a prime example of how major sports are increasingly tapping into the massive appeal of anime and K-pop. For Catzye readers, it highlights the growing mainstream recognition of the genres we love, even reaching the baseball diamond. Keep an eye out for more unique collaborations like this in the future!

title: Jada Toys Drops Invincible Action Figures – With a Two-Year Wait
content:
Fans have been clamoring for Jada Toys' Invincible action figures, and pre-orders are finally live. But hold your horses, because you'll be waiting a while: the first wave isn't expected to arrive until November 2026. Yes, that's two years away.

This 1:12-scale line, inspired by the hit Amazon animated series, kicks off with Mark Grayson, the formidable Conquest, and a standout Kid Omni-Man. After the success of Jada's Street Fighter line, expectations were high for how they'd tackle the brutal world of Invincible. The wait for these figures is long, but the detail looks promising.

The Kid Omni-Man figure, depicting Oliver, particularly impresses. It perfectly captures his animated look with vibrant colors and sharp sculpting. Collectors get five interchangeable faceplates, two hairstyles, and multiple hands for dynamic posing. Each figure is priced at $29.99, featuring the premium articulation fans expect from Jada Toys. It's a significant commitment, but for Invincible die-hards, it just might be worth the wait.
excerpt: Jada Toys has finally opened pre-orders for its highly anticipated 1:12-scale Invincible action figure line, but fans face an unexpected two-year wait until November 2026. The first wave features Mark Grayson, Conquest, and a detailed Kid Omni-Man, all capturing the Amazon series' aesthetic.
imageAlt: Jada Toys 1:12 scale Kid Omni-Man action figure, showing multiple interchangeable parts and dynamic poses.

This could test the patience of even the most dedicated Invincible fans, so definitely keep an eye on updates.

title: Killer Tomatoes Roll Out New Graphic Novel on Kickstarter
content: The absurdity is back! Attack of the Killer Tomatoes, the legendary cult B-movie franchise, is getting a new lease on life. Panick Entertainment and Toybox just launched a Kickstarter for an all-new graphic novel. Fans of the original 1978 film and its equally cheesy sequels, even the Saturday morning cartoon, will recognize the bizarre charm. This property is known for its campy humor and ridiculous premise: sentient, murderous tomatoes. Bringing such a quirky, nostalgic IP into the graphic novel space is an interesting move. It taps into a growing trend of reviving beloved, often overlooked, genre classics for new audiences and long-time fans craving more.
excerpt: The legendary cult B-movie franchise, Attack of the Killer Tomatoes, is making a comeback as a graphic novel. Panick Entertainment and Toybox have launched a Kickstarter campaign for the project, promising fans more of the series' signature absurd humor and sentient fruit.
imageAlt: Cover art for the new Attack of the Killer Tomatoes graphic novel, featuring giant menacing tomatoes.
pullQuote: The absurdity is back! Attack of the Killer Tomatoes, the legendary cult B-movie franchise, is getting a new lease on life.
editorNote: This is a fun one! Fans of quirky retro media will definitely want to check out this Kickstarter. It's cool to see these niche cult classics finding new homes in the graphic novel world, especially with direct fan support.

title: Rick and Morty Co-Creator Dan Harmon: Show Should Run for 100 Years, Until AI Takes Over
content:
Rick and Morty co-creator Dan Harmon has laid out an ambitious vision for the Adult Swim hit: he wants the Emmy-winning series to run for a full century. That's right, a hundred years of dimension-hopping chaos. Harmon recently declared that animated comedies shouldn’t “take a bow” like live-action series. Instead, he believes the job is to be “dragged off kicking and screaming” by Adult Swim, or until AI replaces everyone.

This commitment to endless adventures is front and center as Season 9 nears its end. The latest episode, "Salute Your Morts," tackles a very relatable problem: Morty and Summer have become thoroughly spoiled. Rick, true to form, devises a "perfect" solution. He ships them off to a summer camp for some harsh, real-life lessons, after Beth, fed up with Rick's coddling, insists he deal with the consequences of his own spoiling. It’s classic Rick logic: outsource the problem to an absurd degree.

Harmon's stance on the show's eternal nature is a bold one. Many fans have wondered just how long Rick and Morty can maintain its sharp edge and comedic brilliance. His comments confirm a clear intent: this series isn't going anywhere unless forced off the air. Get ready for potentially many more decades of interdimensional hijinks.
excerpt: Rick and Morty co-creator Dan Harmon has laid out an ambitious vision for the Adult Swim hit: he wants the Emmy-winning series to run for a full century. Harmon argues animated comedies should persist indefinitely, rather than concluding like live-action shows. This philosophy drives the ongoing adventures, even as Season 9 sees Morty and Summer shipped off to camp for being spoiled brats.
imageAlt: Rick Sanchez and Morty Smith looking disgruntled in a camp setting from Rick and Morty S09E09
pullQuote: I think our job is 100 years of Rick and Morty. The show must go on until we all get replaced with AI.
editorNote: This kind of longevity is rare, even for animated shows. Harmon's commitment suggests they're not running out of ideas anytime soon. Fans will be watching to see if the quality can truly endure for decades.

title: The Legendary Batman/Judge Dredd Crossover is Back on Shelves!
content:
The holy grail of comic book crossovers is finally back on shelves! Batman/Judge Dredd: Judgement on Gotham, the legendary clash penned by John Wagner and Alan Grant with art by Simon Bisley, is returning to print. This isn't just any reprint; it's the resurrection of a true benchmark in comic history. Fans have waited years for this.

For those unfamiliar, this 1991 classic brought the grim realities of Gotham City crashing headfirst into the brutal, dystopian future of Mega-City One. Batman, the dark knight of justice, facing off against Judge Dredd, the lawman, judge, jury, and executioner all rolled into one. It's a premise that practically writes itself, a dream match-up that delivered on all fronts. Bisley's distinct, gritty artwork defined the tone, making this a visually unforgettable experience.

The original run became highly sought after, with copies commanding steep prices on the secondary market. Its return ensures a new generation can discover its raw power and thematic depth. This revival also speaks to a wider trend: classic stories finding new life, a welcome development for all global comic enthusiasts, manga included.
excerpt: A legendary comic is finally back! Batman/Judge Dredd: Judgement on Gotham, the seminal 1991 crossover by John Wagner, Alan Grant, and Simon Bisley, is returning to print. Fans can finally get their hands on this iconic clash of worlds without breaking the bank.
imageAlt: Cover art for Batman/Judge Dredd Judgement on Gotham comic showing Batman and Judge Dredd
pullQuote: The holy grail of comic book crossovers is finally back on shelves!
editorNote: This is fantastic news for anyone who appreciates the power of a good crossover. It's a prime example of how two distinct worlds can collide to create something truly special. Hopefully, this paves the way for more forgotten classics to get new life.

title: Power: Origins Teaser Unmasks Young Ghost & Tommy, Promises Gritty NYC Prequel
content:
The "Power" universe isn't slowing down. Starz just unleashed the first official teaser and images for "Power: Origins," its latest prequel. Fans finally get their first glimpse of Spence Moore II as a young "Ghost" and Charlie Mann as a young "Tommy," taking on the iconic roles previously held by Omari Hardwick and Joseph Sikora. This reveal lands as "Power Book III: Raising Kanan" wraps its run, keeping the franchise machine churning.

"Origins" promises a gritty, action-packed dive into the formative years of Ghost, Tommy, and Kanan. Watch them rise as ambitious young entrepreneurs in the unforgiving streets of New York City. title: Marvel Shakes Up Leadership: Cebulski Leads New Manga Division in Japan as Comics Editorial Moves to LA
content:
Massive news from Marvel Comics isn't just about a coast-to-coast move; it's a game-changer for manga fans. Longtime Editor-in-Chief C.B. Cebulski is stepping down to lead a brand-new APAC-focused graphic fiction and manga division, based in Japan. This is huge. It signals a significant, direct investment from Marvel into the booming Asian comics market, with Cebulski's known passion for the medium at the helm.

Meanwhile, Marvel Comics' editorial offices are leaving New York, their home for nearly ninety years. They're heading to Burbank, California, to consolidate with owners Disney and Marvel Studios. The move aims to foster deeper collaboration across film, TV, and comics – the "House of Ideas" all under one roof. Roughly one hundred staffers face relocation within the next year.

It's an ironic shift. Marvel's iconic characters – Spider-Man, Daredevil, the Fantastic Four – are synonymous with New York City. Now, the creators will work from the same coast as DC Comics, which made a similar move over fifteen years ago.

With Cebulski's departure, Stephen Wacker returns to Marvel Comics as the new Editor-in-Chief. Wacker, a veteran editor, understands the comics are the 'source code' for the entire Marvel enterprise. This dual announcement marks a significant restructuring for the comics giant. Fans will watch closely to see how this West Coast consolidation impacts the legendary brand, and how Marvel's manga ambitions truly take off from Japan.
excerpt: In a major strategic shift, Marvel Comics Editor-in-Chief C.B. Cebulski is moving to Japan to lead a new APAC-focused manga and graphic fiction division. This news comes as Marvel's editorial offices are relocating from New York to Burbank, California, consolidating with Disney and Marvel Studios.

With a dedicated division and an experienced leader like Cebulski, expect to see Marvel's presence in Asian comics grow significantly. title: Marvel Shakes Up Leadership: Cebulski Heads to Tokyo for Asia Originals, Wacker Takes EIC
content:
In a seismic strategic pivot, Marvel's Editor-in-Chief C.B. Cebulski is relocating to Tokyo to spearhead the company's ambitious "Asia Originals" initiative. This move places him directly at the forefront of Marvel's expanding manga and local talent partnerships in the region.

Taking his place as EIC is veteran editor Steve Wacker, returning to the publishing helm after a stint in animation. Wacker brings a formidable resume, having overseen influential runs like Matt Fraction's Hawkeye and the introduction of Kamala Khan, Ms. Marvel, a character he’s credited with co-creating. He also shaped Spider-Man's "Brand New Day" era and recently edited Jonathan Hickman’s 3W3M.

Cebulski’s seven-year tenure as EIC profoundly shaped the modern Marvel landscape, from the acclaimed Krakoan Age of X-Men to key manga collaborations like Deadpool Samurai. He was celebrated for his global talent scouting, though his early career included the controversial use of the "Akira Yoshida" pseudonym. Now, he’ll leverage that global eye directly from Japan, nurturing new graphic fiction and connecting with artists across Asia.

Wacker describes his return as a "full-circle moment," eager to add new "floors to the House of Ideas" and confident that "the best Marvel comics have yet to be written." This leadership shuffle underscores Marvel’s dual ambition: maintaining its core comic book strength while making serious, dedicated inroads into the surging global manga and webtoon market. Fans should watch closely as these two industry veterans forge new paths for the House of Ideas.
excerpt: In a significant strategic move, Marvel's Editor-in-Chief C.B. Cebulski is relocating to Tokyo to spearhead the "Asia Originals" initiative, focusing on manga and local talent. Veteran editor Steve Wacker steps in as the new EIC, signaling Marvel's dual commitment to traditional comics and global expansion.

pullQuote: Marvel’s dual ambition: maintaining core comic book strength while making serious inroads into the surging global manga and webtoon market.
editorNote: This leadership change is massive for Marvel, pushing hard into the Asian market with a dedicated EIC-level executive. It’s a clear signal they’re not just dabbling in manga, but making a serious play. Fans should expect a wave of new localized content and creative partnerships.

title: Kingdom of Quartz: Existential Dread Deepens in Latest Volumes
content:
BOMHAT's Kingdom of Quartz plunges readers into a world of existential horror, a reality so chillingly conceived it leaves a lasting mark. We dove into volumes 2-5, and the series only tightens its crystalline grip. This isn't your typical fantasy; it's a meticulously crafted nightmare where the very essence of humanity is questioned.

The premise alone is a gut punch: a world where humans turn to quartz upon death, their remains becoming a resource for the mysterious "Quartz Kingdom." These latest volumes expand on this terrifying ecosystem, revealing the intricate, oppressive societal structures built upon such a grim foundation. BOMHAT's world-building shines, creating a sense of inevitability and dread that permeates every panel. You can feel the weight of this bizarre existence on the characters.

Protagonist Shii's journey becomes increasingly desperate. Her quest to save her brother, who is slowly succumbing to the "quartzification" disease, forces impossible choices. The narrative deftly explores themes of sacrifice, identity, and the blurring lines between life and crystalline death. The artwork, a crucial element, is stark and beautiful, perfectly conveying both the eerie grandeur of the Quartz Kingdom and the raw despair of its inhabitants. It's unsettling yet undeniably captivating.

Volumes 2-5 solidify Kingdom of Quartz as a standout dark fantasy. It's a series for those who crave deep lore, psychological tension, and stories unafraid to confront the bleakest aspects of existence. Prepare to be unnerved.

title: Crimson Abyss #57 Shatters Power Scale: Even Villains Need Saving!
content:
Crimson Abyss just dropped its 57th chapter, and fans are reeling. Mangaka Kaito Aoyama has completely upended the series' established power dynamics, sending shockwaves through the fandom. We thought we knew the ultimate evil, but Aoyama just introduced something far more terrifying.

For dozens of chapters, the Obsidian Hand, with their menacing Dark Mages, represented the pinnacle of villainy in Crimson Abyss. They were a constant, formidable threat, pushing protagonist Ren and his allies to their absolute limits. But in a brutal, unexpected turn, a new entity known only as the Void Manifest has emerged, and it makes the Obsidian Hand look like small-time thugs.

Chapter 57 portrays the Void Manifest's terrifying debut. It systematically dismantles the Obsidian Hand's leadership with chilling efficiency, displaying a level of raw, destructive power and psychological torment that dwarfs anything seen before. The established villains aren't just defeated; they're utterly humiliated, their power rendered irrelevant. This isn't just a new antagonist; it's a fundamental shift in the story's universe. It raises the stakes to an unimaginable level and leaves us wondering how Ren can possibly contend with such an overwhelming force.

title: Legendary Bitchy Bitch Returns to Rattle Cages
content: Roberta Gregory's legendary anti-heroine, Midge McCracken, storms back onto the scene in BITCHY! THE EXASPERATING EXISTENCE OF MIDGE MCCRACKEN. This new collection isn't just another comic; it's a masterclass in unflinching, satirical storytelling. Gregory, a true pioneer in alternative comics, has cultivated Midge's famously cynical and fiercely feminist worldview since the 1980s. For decades, Midge has been the voice for anyone fed up with societal BS, and she's as sharp and relevant as ever. This book is raw, hilarious, and utterly refuses to pull its punches. Fans of boundary-pushing narratives and formidable female protagonists—no matter the medium—will find this volume commands serious attention.
excerpt: Legendary alternative cartoonist Roberta Gregory brings her iconic anti-heroine, Midge McCracken, back in BITCHY! THE EXASPERATING EXISTENCE OF MIDGE MCCRACKEN. This new collection delivers the same unflinching, satirical punch fans have loved since the 80s, offering a raw and hilarious take on the world.

pullQuote: It's raw, it's hilarious, and it absolutely refuses to flinch.
editorNote: This is a major return for one of comics' most enduring and unique voices. Fans who appreciate strong, complex female characters in manga like Nana or Paradise Kiss will find Midge McCracken's unapologetic perspective right up their alley. It's a reminder that truly great storytelling transcends genre.

This isn't just a casual wish; it’s a veteran calling for an unprecedented event, sparking immediate buzz among fans.

Tanaka’s long history with both series gives her words significant weight. Dragon Ball, a foundational pillar of shonen manga by Akira Toriyama, and Eiichiro Oda's One Piece, a global phenomenon, are both produced by Toei Animation. While the franchises have touched before, notably in the "Dream 9 Toriko & One Piece & Dragon Ball Z Super Collaboration Special," that was a one-off. Tanaka specifically envisions a dedicated, full-length anime series bringing these worlds together properly.

Imagine Luffy's boundless energy clashing with Goku's raw power, or Zoro facing off against Piccolo. Tanaka’s public statement could be the spark needed for Toei to seriously consider such a monumental project. Fans have been fantasizing about this for decades. Her voice carries the history of both sagas, making her plea resonate deeply. This isn't just fan service; it’s a potential industry-defining event.

title: Political Demands Sink Dark Horse's Holocaust Book
content:
Dark Horse Comics reportedly pulled the plug on a new edition of Cartoonists Against The Holocaust, sparking a heated controversy that sends shivers down the spine. Author Dr. Rafael Medoff, a respected Holocaust scholar, alleges the publisher canceled the book after he flat-out refused editor Craig Yoe's demands. Yoe, Medoff claims, insisted on injecting criticisms of Israel and the US into the introduction, accusing Israel of "war crimes" in Gaza and the Trump administration of "concentration-style prisons" for migrants.

Medoff did not mince words. He called these demands "falsehoods" that would politicize a vital historical work and diminish the horrific suffering of Holocaust victims. "There are no concentration camps in America," he stressed, warning against misusing such terms. He further branded the demand to denounce Israel as "antisemitic bullying." Medoff insists Dark Horse had already accepted the book, contract in hand, and scheduled it for a 2026 release. Everything was ready for production until Yoe's "outrageous political demands" surfaced.

Dark Horse, through legal counsel Philip Simon, offered a contrasting explanation to the New York Post. Simon cited Yoe's failure to meet scheduling and the company's "financial needs" as reasons for the cancellation. Intriguingly, Craig Yoe is no longer working with Dark Horse after this incident. Yoe himself only vaguely acknowledged "a number of errors" in Medoff's account without elaborating.

Medoff isn't buying Dark Horse's official line. He points out he'd secured a large advance order and significant promotional support from Jewish organizations and Holocaust studies professors. For him, the only "scheduling" snag was Yoe's refusal to proceed without the mandated political content.

Cartoonists Against The Holocaust sought to chronicle the courageous efforts of American political cartoonists, like Dr. Seuss, who bravely spoke out against Nazi atrocities. This entire debacle raises serious questions about editorial integrity and creator autonomy in an increasingly charged political landscape.
excerpt: Dark Horse Comics reportedly cancelled a new edition of Cartoonists Against The Holocaust after author Dr. Rafael Medoff refused editor Craig Yoe's demands to include criticisms of Israel and the US. Medoff, a Holocaust scholar, called the demands "falsehoods" and "antisemitic bullying." The publisher cited scheduling and financial issues, but Medoff maintains the political demands were the real reason.
imageAlt: Cover art for Cartoonists Against The Holocaust book, showing historical political cartoons.
entities: The David S. Wyman Institute for Holocaust Studies
pullQuote: Requiring a Holocaust scholar to denounce Israel to see his book published is antisemitic bullying.
editorNote: This situation is a stark reminder of the pressures creators and publishers face today. Fans will want to watch how this unfolds, especially concerning editorial independence and the handling of sensitive historical topics. It's a tough line to walk.
