title: Kripke Goes Dark: John Ross Bowie Teases Shocking Turn in TBBT Spinoff
content:
Fans of The Big Bang Theory's snarky, rhotacism-afflicted rival Barry Kripke better brace themselves. John Ross Bowie, the actor behind the character, is back for HBO Max's Stuart Fails to Save the Universe—and Kripke is taking a surprisingly dark turn. This isn't the same antagonist fans remember from Caltech.

The new series sees Bowie's Kripke join TBBT regulars Kevin Sussman (Stuart Bloom), Brian Posehn (Bert Kibbler), and Lauren Lapkus (Denise) in an unlikely ensemble. This "The Big Bang Theory meets Sliders" premise throws the foursome into an apocalyptic scenario. They stumble upon a trans-dimensional device, launching them into alternate realities with Stuart somehow tasked to save the universe. It's a significant genre shift for the franchise, pushing familiar characters into uncharted sci-fi territory.

Bowie admits slipping back into Kripke's skin was "distressingly easy," noting the plasma physicist's "tasteless and filterless" nature quickly resurfaced. Despite Kripke's limited interactions with this group in the original series, Bowie found chemistry with his new co-stars immediate, having known Sussman, Posehn, and Lapkus for years through various comedy circuits. He even calls them "the funniest cast I've ever been in."

What truly stands out is Kripke's evolution. Bowie was "taken aback" by an "alarming" act Kripke commits early on, one that "very much disrupts the canon" of the original Big Bang Theory. The writers, however, ensure there are consequences. Kripke faces a beatdown for his misdeeds, a rare choreographed fight scene for Bowie that he describes as a "new frontier." This promises a more complex, perhaps even morally ambiguous, Kripke than we've ever seen.

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe premieres July 23rd on HBO Max, with new episodes weekly.

title: President Curtis Spinoff Confirms Rick & Morty Cameo, Reveals Major Character Retcon
content: President Curtis, the upcoming Rick and Morty spinoff, will feature the titular duo in its opening episode. But don't expect them to stick around. Executive Producers Dan Harmon and James Siciliano confirm Rick and Morty's appearance is a "one and done" for the season. This is a deliberate choice, intended to let the new series forge its own identity. This isn't just a brief diversion; it's a calculated move to separate President Curtis from its parent show, giving the political satire room to breathe. The July 26th premiere introduces President Andre Curtis, voiced by the inimitable Keith David, and his eclectic White House staff. This includes Stephanie Beatriz's Chief of Staff Banks and Jim Rash's Special Agent O'Doyle. They're tasked with the interdimensional and paranormal crises that Rick Sanchez would find beneath his cosmic pay grade. Harmon and Siciliano reveal a significant retcon for Curtis's character. In Rick and Morty, he often sought approval. For the spinoff, they've flipped that completely. "He is almost the opposite," Siciliano states, emphasizing Curtis's commitment to duty. This President isn't playing politics for numbers; he's doing the job because "if he doesn't, someone worse will." Harmon paints him as a "golden retriever" type, someone people inherently trust, who begrudgingly accepts leadership. His strategic ex-wife, his "Yoda," is no longer in the picture. This leaves him to navigate complex alien diplomacy and cryptid hunts with a soldier's unwavering resolve, rather than a politician's cunning. This self-contained approach was key to choosing Curtis for a spinoff. Harmon compares it to Doctor Who and The X-Files — both deal with aliens, but from distinct perspectives. President Curtis aims for a similar tonal consistency without being redundant to Rick's broader, more chaotic exploits. It's a smart play, carving out a unique niche within the sprawling multiverse of Adult Swim animation.

The show aims to explore interdimensional crises with a duty-bound, "golden retriever" leader, distinctly separate from Rick Sanchez's chaotic exploits.

Fans will be curious to see how this 'retconned,' duty-driven President tackles universal threats without Rick's nihilistic genius. It’s a bold direction for the Rick and Morty universe, and we're here for it.

title: Masamune Shirow's Ghost in the Shell: Our Cyberpunk Present
content:
Ghost in the Shell wasn't just groundbreaking cyberpunk manga; it was a stark warning, a crystal ball peering decades into our future. Masamune Shirow's seminal work, first published in 1989, didn't just imagine a world of full-body prosthetics and sentient AI. It eerily predicted the very real ethical dilemmas we grapple with today.

Consider Major Motoko Kusanagi's cybernetic body. What once seemed pure fantasy—replacing organic limbs with advanced machinery, enhancing human capabilities beyond natural limits—is now on the cusp of reality. Advanced prosthetics already offer incredible functionality, blurring the line between man and machine. The debate around neural implants and brain-computer interfaces, once confined to sci-fi, is rapidly accelerating.

Then there's the concept of "ghost hacking"—manipulating memories and identities within a vast digital network. Shirow envisioned a world where one's very sense of self could be digitally altered or stolen. Today, deepfakes and sophisticated digital misinformation campaigns prove just how fragile our perception of reality can be. The fight for data privacy and the integrity of information is a constant, urgent battle.

And Project 2501, the Puppet Master, a self-aware entity born from the internet's depths? We're not quite there with fully sentient AI, but the rapid advancements in large language models and generative AI systems force us to confront similar questions. What defines consciousness? What are the rights of an emergent intelligence?

Shirow's genius lay in understanding not just the tech, but its profound societal and philosophical implications. Ghost in the Shell remains relevant because its "future shock" is our present. Its world of ubiquitous networks, enhanced humans, and digital identity crises isn't just entertainment; it's a mirror.
excerpt: Masamune Shirow's iconic Ghost in the Shell manga wasn't just cyberpunk entertainment; it was a startlingly accurate prediction of our technological future. From advanced cybernetic prosthetics to the chilling implications of digital identity manipulation and emergent AI, GITS eerily anticipated our modern world and its ethical challenges.
imageAlt: Cover art for Ghost in the Shell manga volume 1 showing Major Motoko Kusanagi
pullQuote: Masamune Shirow's seminal work eerily predicted the very real ethical dilemmas we grapple with today.
editorNote: This piece highlights why Ghost in the Shell remains so vital. It's not just a classic; it's a conversation starter about our tech-driven reality. Fans should revisit the manga and original film, then compare its themes to current events. The questions it poses about humanity, identity, and technology are more urgent than ever.

title: Criminal Minds' Kirsten Vangsness Reveals Secret, Unpaid Cameo in "The Studio" Season 2
content:
Criminal Minds veteran Kirsten Vangsness just dropped a surprise that reveals a dedication to craft rarely seen from established stars. She quietly secured an uncredited, unpaid background role in the upcoming second season of Apple TV+'s acclaimed series, "The Studio."

Vangsness joined the set as an ambulance worker, purely for the learning experience. She openly admitted bidding on an online auction for the opportunity, wanting to immerse herself in a new production environment. "Nobody knew that I was on 'Criminal Minds,'" she recounted, donning contacts to avoid recognition. She found herself in scenes with big names like Seth Rogen and Kathryn Hahn, gaining invaluable insight into a different kind of set.

This wasn't her only recent acting challenge. Vangsness also reflected on her recent appearance in the Scrubs revival episode, "My Angel." Playing Pauline, a patient desperately needing a liver transplant, was a stark contrast to her usual confident Criminal Minds persona. She described the experience as "terrifying," akin to "acting school," given the unique shooting style and the talent of the Scrubs cast, including Sarah Chalke. Vangsness even hopes Pauline might return with the puppy she planned to adopt.

This dedication to growing as an actor, even after years in the spotlight, is genuinely inspiring. It's a reminder that true artists never stop honing their skills, no matter their level of fame.

Next, "Designing the Future" dives into Trek's iconic aesthetic. Panelists will explore how artists defined the look of tomorrow across six decades. Rare materials from the Roddenberry Archive promise a fascinating visual journey.

Perhaps most intriguing is "Making Contact." Roddenberry Entertainment teams up with NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory scientists. They’ll break down what making contact with alien civilizations might truly entail. It's a bold fusion of sci-fi fantasy and concrete scientific reality. This ambitious approach sets these panels apart, offering a thoughtful, celebratory look at a foundational sci-fi phenomenon.

Beyond the main awards, the evening also includes the presentation of the Bob Clampett Humanitarian Award and the Bill Finger Award for Excellence in Comic Book Writing, further recognizing significant contributions to the industry. title: The Sims 4 Delivers Long-Awaited Performance Fixes and AutoSave
content:
The Sims 4 is finally getting the quality-of-life overhaul fans have demanded for years. Maxis and Electronic Arts just dropped a massive update, pulling long-awaited features directly from their "Laundry List"—a clear response to community feedback. Say goodbye to lost progress; AutoSave and Save Reminders are here to rescue your precious Sim stories. This isn't just a minor patch; it's a foundational shift for a game that's seen its share of frustrations.

The real star of the show? Memory Boost. Launching July 21st across all platforms, this feature fundamentally changes how The Sims 4 manages its memory. We're talking smoother gameplay, better frame rates, reduced lag, quicker loading screens, and far fewer crashes. This is huge, especially for players with sprawling legacies, massive builds, or older, memory-heavy save files. Players have been begging for this for ages, and the impact will be immediate.

AutoSave now works quietly in the background, creating save points at key moments. You can even customize its frequency. Prefer a hands-on approach? Save Reminders will prompt manual saves. No more accidental rage-quits erasing your architectural masterpieces. It's about time these core safeguards were implemented.

While this update focused on building crucial new systems, the developers promise more. Their Quality of Life team has spent months tackling community-voted issues from UI glitches to build mode annoyances. And a significant September update looms, promising smarter, more consistent Sim autonomy. This sustained commitment to player experience and long-term stability is a welcome direction for The Sims 4. Maxis is finally listening, and the game is poised for a much smoother, more reliable future.

This massive overhaul targets long-standing performance issues, lag, and lost progress, promising a much smoother experience for all Simmers.

title: Jorge Gutiérrez Kills Amazon AI Series in 72 Hours Amid Artist Backlash
content:

Gutiérrez, the acclaimed creator behind The Book of Life, made an unprecedented move: he pulled his new animated series Punky Duck from an Amazon AI-funded program just 72 hours after its announcement. He declared himself "the first creator to kill their own show a day and a half after announcing it." It was a swift, dramatic capitulation following intense fan outcry.

Fans were aghast when Amazon's GenAI Creators' Fund listed Gutiérrez, a vocal artist advocate, among its initial projects. This felt like a betrayal. He initially defended his participation, hoping to ensure "artists driving tech," drawn by the appeal of a quick greenlight for an original idea.

But the backlash was fierce and immediate. Anger escalated, even drawing death threats against his family. The pressure became untenable. Gutiérrez publicly withdrew Punky Duck. "Actions speak louder than words," he stated, apologizing for upsetting anyone.

Reflecting on the storm, Gutiérrez told Variety he genuinely aimed to give artists a voice in emerging tech. But he quickly realized the AI debate is "black-and-white." His "good intentions" inadvertently led his family to "hell." Amazon, he noted, supported his decision. Gutiérrez fears AI will advance regardless, leaving artists out of crucial discussions. It's a sobering outlook for the industry.

title: Nolan's Odyssey: Grand Scope, Star Power, But Does It Lack Heart?
content:
Christopher Nolan's long-anticipated live-action adaptation of Homer's The Odyssey is finally here, and it’s… good. But for a director synonymous with cinematic grandeur, "good" just might not be enough. While the film majestically captures the epic's vast scope, it ultimately falls short of the greatness fans expected, struggling under the weight of ambition and some surprising creative missteps.

Adapting Homer's The Odyssey is a Herculean task. It's an ancient epic, known to all but notoriously difficult to translate to screen. Nolan, admirably, tries to make it accessible, tackling its massive scope with his signature visual prowess. Clocking in at just under three hours, the runtime is surprisingly lean for such an expansive tale. The film embraces a non-linear, almost episodic structure, presenting Odysseus's trials as self-contained fables. This creative choice largely works, keeping the audience engaged through its meandering journey home, much like how ancient myths were orally shared.

Yet, this fragmented narrative comes at a cost. The film struggles to build genuine emotional investment in Odysseus's plight. While Matt Damon delivers a powerful, late-game monologue that salvages some emotional payoff, the narrative mostly tells us about his longing for home rather than letting us feel it. The dire situation in Ithaca, with Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and Telemachus (Tom Holland) besieged by arrogant suitors, feels underdeveloped. We don't fully grasp their desperate circumstances, leaving us emotionally detached from their struggle.

Performances are a clear highlight. Robert Pattinson shines as the insufferable Antinous, proving once again he can embody pure villainy. Matt Damon carries the weight of Odysseus, while Anne Hathaway and Tom Holland make the most of their limited screentime. Samantha Morton delivers a chilling performance as Circe, and Ludwig Göransson's score is, predictably, a triumph.

Here's the rub: Nolan's signature commitment to stark realism often clashes with the fantastical, mythological core of The Odyssey. Audiences are already debating "historical accuracy" for a story about Cyclops and Sirens, which frankly misses the point entirely. This dissonance extends to the dialogue, which sometimes feels too modern against the epic backdrop, and the film’s reluctance to fully embrace the horror or surreal elements inherent in the source material.

Ultimately, Nolan's Odyssey is a technically impressive, visually stunning adaptation. It's a testament to his ambition. But in attempting to ground a myth in his signature realism, Nolan inadvertently hobbles its emotional impact and its ability to truly soar. It's a good film, perhaps even a very good one, but it won't be remembered as a classic on par with Homer's timeless epic.
excerpt: Christopher Nolan's live-action The Odyssey delivers on epic scope and boasts standout performances, but its commitment to realism clashes with the mythical source. Despite its visual grandeur, the film struggles to build deep emotional investment, leaving it a technically impressive but ultimately imperfect adaptation of Homer's timeless tale.
imageAlt: Promotional key art for Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey film, featuring Odysseus on a ship amidst stormy seas with mythical creatures faintly visible.
pullQuote: Nolan's signature commitment to stark realism often clashes with the fantastical, mythological core of The Odyssey.
editorNote: This review highlights a recurring challenge for live-action adaptations of epic, fantastical stories. While Nolan's vision is always ambitious, fans might wonder if some tales are best served with a touch more unbridled imagination. It’s a fascinating look at where realism meets myth.

Metzger, a mutant with unique abilities, appeared without any acknowledgment or apparent payment to his original creators. Such incidents are unfortunately common, where characters become part of a publisher's vast catalog, often used in new stories far removed from their origins, leaving original creators out in the cold.

This issue isn't confined to Western comics. It's a familiar refrain across creative industries, including manga and anime. From mangaka fighting for proper royalties to animators struggling for fair wages and recognition for their conceptual work, the battle for creator rights is universal. It underscores a systemic challenge where corporations benefit immensely from the ingenuity of individual artists, sometimes without adequate compensation or credit.

Joe Casey's public stance is a powerful reminder. It highlights the ongoing need for greater transparency and fairer practices. Creators everywhere deserve proper acknowledgment and payment for the worlds and characters they bring to life.

title: Blue Beetle Lives! Xolo Maridueña Confirmed for James Gunn's Superman
content:
Hold the phone, DC fans! Xolo Maridueña is officially back as Blue Beetle. The actor will reprise his role as Jaime Reyes in James Gunn's highly anticipated Superman film, Man of Tomorrow, set to hit theaters July 9, 2027.

This is huge news. The 2023 Blue Beetle solo film, while a critical darling and a fresh take on superhero origin stories, faced an uphill battle at the box office. Fans worried if Maridueña's nuanced portrayal of Jaime Reyes would ever fit into the new DC Universe crafted by James Gunn and Peter Safran. Now, those fears are laid to rest.

Gunn's DC Studios is busy forging a new, cohesive cinematic universe. Bringing back a beloved character and actor from the previous regime isn't just a nod to continuity; it's a significant vote of confidence. It opens up fascinating questions about how specific elements from the prior DC Extended Universe might weave into this fresh narrative. We're eager to see what role Blue Beetle plays alongside David Corenswet's Superman.

This surprise announcement confirms the character's place in the new DC Universe, a significant win for fans who loved the 2023 solo movie. It's a huge shift for DC Studios' continuity plans.

title: Fugitive Doctor's Sonic Screwdriver "Controversy" Gets Canon-Approved Answer
content:
Doctor Who fans went into a tizzy over the Fugitive Doctor's new Sonic Screwdriver in the "Circuit Breaker" crossover. "Canon violation!" cried some. "She can't be the earliest Doctor!" wailed others. But a swift, clear explanation from BBC Studios Brand Manager James Page has shut down the manufactured outrage.

Page, also a producer for "Circuit Breaker," clarified for Radio Times that the story unfolds after the Fugitive Doctor (Jo Martin) rejected a sonic when she met the Thirteenth Doctor. In "Circuit Breaker," she's working alongside UNIT scientists Osgood and Andrew. These two admire the Doctor and urge her to adopt more conventional methods – including the sonic screwdriver. This creates a compelling narrative tension. The Fugitive Doctor is fiercely independent, but she's challenged to reconsider her approach.

This isn't a plot hole; it's character development. This evolving dynamic will eventually explain her carrying the device. Fans will get more answers in "The Kaleidoscope," a story co-written by Jo Martin herself, and through the UNIT HQ website. Page also confirmed UNIT still considers her the "earliest known incarnation," preserving her mysterious origins. "Circuit Breaker" directly follows "Fugitive of the Judoon," anchoring it firmly in established continuity.

So, breathe easy, Whovians. This isn't a retcon. It's a deliberate narrative choice, building on the Fugitive Doctor's complex journey. And with Jo Martin's direct involvement in crafting these stories, we're in for an exciting ride.
excerpt: The Fugitive Doctor's new Sonic Screwdriver in the "Circuit Breaker" event sent some Doctor Who fans into a canon-fueled frenzy. However, BBC's James Page offers a clear, character-driven explanation, confirming the device's appearance is part of an ongoing narrative arc, not a retcon. Fans can expect more details in upcoming stories, including one co-written by Jo Martin herself.
imageAlt: Jo Martin as the Fugitive Doctor, holding a Sonic Screwdriver in a futuristic setting.
pullQuote: This isn't a retcon; it's character development unfolding in real time.
editorNote: This clarification from BBC Studios is exactly what fans needed to understand the Fugitive Doctor's evolving arc. It's especially exciting to see Jo Martin herself co-writing "The Kaleidoscope," which suggests a deep commitment to her character's unique place in Doctor Who lore. Fans should definitely keep an eye on how this storyline develops.

title: Andy Serkis's Gollum Film Officially Begins Production
content:
Andy Serkis has officially started filming The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum, stepping back into the iconic role and behind the camera. This is a massive live-action return to Middle-earth, spearheaded by the master of motion capture himself. Fans have waited years for more news, and now production is officially underway.

Serkis directs and stars, with franchise architects Peter Jackson, Fran Walsh, and Philippa Boyens producing and writing. The story bridges the gap between Bilbo's birthday and the journey to Moria, focusing on Aragorn and Gandalf's search for Gollum and the One Ring. It's a key period in Middle-earth lore.

One significant detail clarified: The Hunt for Gollum is a single film, not two. However, Warner Bros. is indeed developing a separate, second live-action Lord of the Rings project. We're looking at a December 17, 2027 release for Serkis's vision.

title: Absolute Flash #17: Brainiac Turns Lex Luthor's World Into a Chainsaw Nightmare
content:
DC Comics' Absolute universe takes a truly brutal turn in Absolute Flash #17, delivering a shocking origin story for an alternate Lex Luthor. Brainiac, ever the puppet master, tortures Luthor by forcing him to watch his family get murdered with chainsaws. His goal? To break the happy, unassuming Lex Luthor of this parallel world and forge him into a new, twisted villain for an "Absolute Evil Justice League."

This isn't your standard Lex Luthor. In the Absolute universe, he’s been living an idyllic rural life, even sporting a full head of hair. Brainiac, following intelligence from the Absolute Mirror Master, sought out this different Luthor. Now, he's using unimaginable cruelty to mold him into a familiar partnership – but one born from pure trauma. This pushes the boundaries even for the grimdark "Absolute" imprint.

Meanwhile, the main focus of Absolute Flash #17 centers on Wally West. After seventeen issues, he finally gets a superhero name and discovers new abilities, including a healing factor. He and the Rogues are battling to free Colorado from Grodd's grip, adding another layer of chaos to this darker DC landscape.

Jeff Lemire and Haining helm Absolute Flash #17, while Jason Aaron and Juan Ferreyra guide the parallel horrors unfolding in Absolute Superman. This shared universe is clearly not pulling any punches.

This horrific event aims to transform Luthor into a new supervillain for an "Absolute Evil Justice League." Simultaneously, Wally West gains a new superhero identity and powers amidst the chaos.

title: Captain America Debates Democracy with Doctor Doom... In Hell?!
content:
The latest issues of Marvel's Armageddon event just dropped, and writer Chip Zdarsky is pulling no punches. Forget the earthly battles; Captain America is currently debating the very concept of democracy with Doctor Doom. Their unlikely philosophical clash? None other than literal Hell. It’s a jaw-dropping twist that sets a dark, intriguing tone.

Back on Earth, General Ross, the notorious Red Hulk, is enacting his brutal vision of global "democracy" using a Hulked-Up U.S. Army. This cynical satire on interventionism has Ross deploying Doctor Doom's future-predicting tech to wipe out all opposition. He envisioned a future where he reigns supreme, but his plans are already crumbling.

First, a new Captain America recruit, David Colton, suddenly gains cosmic-level powers from long-lost Ultimate Universe tech. This Sentry-tier upgrade was completely unforeseen by Ross. Then, in a stunning reversal, Ross himself is captured by Russian forces. His carefully predicted future shattered, the architect of forced democracy now finds himself a pawn in a larger, even more unsettling geopolitical game. Zdarsky is pushing Marvel into truly audacious territory.
excerpt: Captain America finds himself debating democracy with Doctor Doom in literal Hell, while on Earth, Red Hulk's plans to forcibly spread his vision of "democracy" take an unexpected turn when he's captured by Russian forces. The Armageddon event is shaking up the Marvel Universe with shocking twists and ideological battles orchestrated by writer Chip Zdarsky.
imageAlt: Captain America, Doctor Doom, and Red Hulk characters from Marvel Comics
pullQuote: Captain America is busy debating the merits of democracy with Doctor Doom in literal Hell.
editorNote: This event isn't just big for Marvel; it's a bold satirical take on global politics, something we've seen increasingly in manga and anime too. Fans should definitely watch how Zdarsky ties these wild threads together, especially with Russia's involvement. It raises uncomfortable questions about power and ideology.

title: Kaketa Tsuki no Mercedes Anime: Set for an Unprecedented Winter 2027 Premiere
content:
Hold onto your fangs, anime fans! We just got major news for Kaketa Tsuki no Mercedes, but there's a catch: the TV anime adaptation won't drop until Winter 2027. Yes, you read that right — a full three-year wait for this vampire-dungeon fantasy to hit screens.

Hakuhodo DY Music & Pictures kicked off the official site this week, treating us to the first promo video, key staff, and lead cast for the series, officially titled Mercedes and the Waning Moon: The Dungeoneering Feats of a Discarded Vampire Aristocrat. It's a mouthful, but the premise is intriguing.

Studio DEEN takes the reins on this one. Kenichi Imaizumi, known for his directorial work on Myriad Colors Phantom World, is at the helm. Michiko Yokote, a veteran talent behind series composition for hits like Shirobako, handles the script — a promising sign for the narrative quality. Mariko Komatsu designs the characters, while Tsubasa Ito composes the score.

For voice talent, we're getting Yui Ogura as the titular Mercedes and Reina Ueda as Stella. Both are fantastic picks, bringing a wealth of experience and range to their roles.

The story itself is another reincarnation fantasy, but with a unique bite: Mercedes, a former human, is reborn as a vampire noble. Deemed incompetent, she's unceremoniously dumped in a dungeon. Her only path to survival and proving her worth? Conquer the dungeon. It's a fresh take on the crowded isekai genre, and could stand out if handled with care.

Firehead's original light novel series, illustrated by Oumi, is published by Kodansha K Lanove Books. Three volumes are currently available, giving fans plenty of material to dive into during the lengthy wait.

title: Absolute Solomon Grundy's Eyeball-Packed Debut Shocks Absolute Green Arrow #3
content:
Absolute Solomon Grundy? Yes, you read that right. DC's "Absolute Green Arrow #3" just landed, and it unleashed a genuinely shocking new take on the classic zombie villain. This isn't your grandad's Grundy; this version bursts onto the scene with a horrifying body quite literally full of eyes, a grotesque echo of the unsettling finds from previous issues. And in a clever, chilling nod to his iconic nursery rhyme origin, he’s “born on a Wednesday” – today, as it happens.

This issue, crafted by Pornsak Pichetshote and Rafael Albuquerque, deepens the twisted "Absolute Universe" narrative. This new DC imprint ruthlessly reimagines established heroes and villains, twisting their lore into darker, more cynical forms. Oliver Queen is a killer. Star City is unraveling. While fans might have expected other familiar faces, Grundy’s unexpected, horrifying arrival is a bold statement.

Beyond Grundy, the issue is packed with more familiar names reborn through this dark lens. We get the first "Absolute" mention of Emiko Queen, Oliver's half-sister and a former Red Arrow. Roy Harper, the original Speedy, is now a prime suspect in Oliver's killing spree, with Black Canary hot on his trail after he was seen digging a grave. Even minor characters like Brittany Brandon, originally the vigilante Moonbow, reappear as a podcaster, far from her affluent vigilante past.

The "Absolute" line thrives on unsettling reversals. Reese Tyler, a pharmaceutical CEO from earlier issues, is dead. But his father is now confirmed as Rex Tyler – the original Hourman – reimagined not as a Miraclo-powered hero, but as a chemist pursuing immortality. Joker, now trillionaire Jack Grimm, apparently already cracked that code. Even Vlatava, the homeland of Count Vertigo, gets a nod, hinting at more villainous debuts down the line.

This series clearly isn't holding back. It's an aggressive, character-twisting reinvention, and Grundy’s debut proves there are no sacred cows in this dark new world.
excerpt: Absolute Solomon Grundy makes a terrifying, unexpected debut in "Absolute Green Arrow #3," featuring a grotesque body full of eyes and a chilling nod to his iconic origin. The issue, by Pornsak Pichetshote and Rafael Albuquerque, deepens the dark "Absolute Universe" narrative, twisting established DC lore and character origins for a grim new era.
imageAlt: Cover art for Absolute Green Arrow #3, featuring a dark illustration of Green Arrow and other characters.
pullQuote: This isn't your grandad's Grundy; this version bursts onto the scene with a horrifying body quite literally full of eyes.
editorNote: This "Absolute Universe" is really leaning into the horror, isn't it? Solomon Grundy's new design is a far cry from his classic lumbering form, fitting perfectly into the series' grim tone. Fans watching this line will want to see which other iconic DC characters get the "Absolute" treatment next – and how twisted they become.

title: The 5 Day: Reading Wednesday's Manga & Anime News Through the Number of Change
content:
Today's Number: 5

On Wednesday, July 15, 2026, the day's headlines arrive under the sign of the 5 — the numerologist's number of change, a vibration of freedom, disruption, and restless movement. It is a useful lens, if only a literary one, for reading a news cycle led this morning by "G.I. JOE #24 Unleashes Energon: A Game-Changer for the Iconic Franchise?." Strip away the mysticism and the number still works as a mood: the stories crossing the wire share a common temperature, and today that temperature reads as change.

Set "G.I. JOE #24 Unleashes Energon: A Game-Changer for the Iconic Franchise?" beside "Invincible Universe: Battle Beast #11 Kicks Off Round Two of Brutal Fight" and a thread begins to show. The two stories come from different desks — perhaps different corners of the industry — yet both turn on the same underlying tension that the 5 tends to surface: the pull between what is being started and what is being held together. Read together rather than apart, the day's lead items stop looking like isolated announcements and start looking like a single weather system.

The Connective Thread

Beneath the lead, the supporting stories — "Fujimoto's Look Back Live-Action Film Sets September 11 Premiere, Unveils Star-Studded Cast", "Ashley Johnson Reveals Terrifying Kidnap Attempt During Growing Pains Filming", "Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 to Host SDCC 2026 Panel, Still No Release Date", "Megami Tensei Creator Delivers Personal English Novel Translation" — fill in the pattern. Coverage from Bleeding Cool and Anime News Network keeps circling the same themes: franchises under strain, decisions deferred, and the quiet recalculation of who holds the initiative. None of these stories was written with the others in mind, which is precisely why their convergence is worth noting. The job of analysis is to read the cycle as a whole, and the whole, today, leans hard into change.

Catzye scanned 40 headlines across the major manga and anime feeds today. Of those, 3 carry titles that reduce, letter by letter, to today's number 5. That is a coincidence of language rather than fate — but it is the kind of coincidence that makes you look twice, and looking twice is the whole point of reading the news slowly.

Among those number-5 headlines: "Chiho Saitō's VS Lupin Manga Concludes After A Decade-Long Run"; "Sea Witch Showdown: Ursula Battles Sisters for Triton's Trident in Series Finale"; "Lestat Rocks Out: Vampire Lestat Concert Special Streams on AMC+". Whatever you make of the arithmetic, the stories themselves reward attention. Each one, in its way, is a story about freedom, disruption, and restless movement — which is to say, a story about the choices facing the people in it.

What To Watch

If the 5 is the number of change, then the test of the next few days is whether today's openings are followed through or quietly abandoned. Numerology would call that the difference between the number's higher and lower expression. A journalist would just call it the follow-up — the second-day story that tells you whether the first one mattered. Either way, the questions are the same: who acts, who waits, and who pays for the delay.

Catzye's daily analysis reads the news through the lens of the day's number. It is not a forecast. It is a way of paying attention — a reminder that the headlines, however scattered, tend to rhyme. Check back tomorrow, when the number turns over and the pattern shifts with it.

A Note on Method

Every headline on this page was pulled from our newsroom feeds and reduced using standard Pythagorean numerology — each letter mapped to a digit one through nine, summed by word, then reduced until a single digit or master number remains. The same arithmetic that gives a name its Destiny number gives a headline its vibration. We make no claim that the universe arranges the news to suit a number. We claim only that a constraint, even an arbitrary one, is a good way to force fresh attention onto stories you might otherwise scroll past — and that the day's events, read together, almost always tell a more coherent story than any one of them does alone.

title: Invincible Universe: Battle Beast #11 Kicks Off Round Two of Brutal Fight
content:

Image Comics confirms this epic showdown is spilling into a second issue, much to the delight of fans who crave over-the-top superhero violence.

The preview pages show Battle Beast taking a truly devastating punishment. Conquest, ever the confident sadist, sneers about his opponent's inability to inflict damage. But Battle Beast, true to form, refuses to yield. This is the kind of relentless, high-stakes combat Invincible readers live for.

Robert Kirkman pens the script, continuing his deep dive into the Invincible Universe's most savage corners. title: Fujimoto's Look Back Live-Action Film Sets September 11 Premiere, Unveils Star-Studded Cast
content:
Tatsuki Fujimoto's acclaimed one-shot Look Back is officially headed to the big screen on September 11, 2026, in a live-action adaptation. A new trailer drop confirms the premiere date and introduces a stellar expanded cast, injecting major talent into an already highly anticipated film.

Masaki Suda, a powerhouse known for roles in Gintama and Death Note, joins the lineup. So does Kankurō Kudō, a revered figure in Japanese entertainment as an actor, screenwriter, and director. They join Kayo Noro, Ryō Ikeda, Miyu Sasaki, and Maho Yamada. This impressive ensemble rounds out a cast led by Yuumi Kawai as Fujino and Mizuki Yoshida as Kyomoto, the two aspiring manga artists at the story's core.

Fans of Fujimoto's Chainsaw Man know his knack for intense, character-driven narratives. Look Back, his 2021 Shonen Jump+ phenomenon, captivated readers with its raw emotional depth, exploring themes of friendship, loss, and the isolating pursuit of art. Adapting such a beloved, poignant work is a massive undertaking.

Directing and scripting the film is Kenji Kamiyama, a veteran whose credits include Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex and Napping Princess. His involvement strongly suggests a nuanced adaptation. The trailer hints at Kamiyama's vision, building excitement for a faithful yet fresh take on Fujimoto's masterpiece.
excerpt: Tatsuki Fujimoto's acclaimed one-shot Look Back gets a live-action film adaptation premiering September 11, 2026. The new trailer revealed a stellar expanded cast including Masaki Suda and Kankurō Kudō, joining leads Yuumi Kawai and Mizuki Yoshida. Kenji Kamiyama directs this highly anticipated film.
imageAlt: Key visual for the live-action Look Back film, showing the main characters Fujino and Kyomoto, with cast names.

title: Ashley Johnson Reveals Terrifying Kidnap Attempt During Growing Pains Filming
content:
Before she voiced iconic characters in Critical Role, The Last of Us, and countless animated series, Ashley Johnson faced a terrifying ordeal as a child star. The beloved voice actor recently shared a chilling account of a near-kidnapping on the set of the 90s sitcom Growing Pains. It happened during her very first year on the show, she revealed on her podcast, Weird Kids, co-hosted with Taliesin Jaffe.

Security on the Warner Bros lot was dramatically different then. Actors would walk past the studio audience, often within mere feet of fans. Johnson recalled a grim threat letter: "Somebody had written in and said that, 'I am coming to set and I am going to bring a gun and I am going to murder some of the cast.'"

Then, the unthinkable happened. While walking with her mother, a man suddenly "hops out of the line and he grabs me and grabs me up and starts booking it." Johnson, just a child, was reportedly confused, even politely asking, "Who are you, sir?" as she was carried away. The fan was high on an unknown substance and was packing a gun.

Thankfully, security intervened swiftly, apprehending the armed fan. Johnson was flung during the scuffle, her biggest concern afterward being that she might be "in trouble" herself. It's a stark, horrifying glimpse into the dangers child actors faced in a less secure era. Johnson's resilience shines through, making her subsequent rise as a voice acting powerhouse even more remarkable.
excerpt: Voice acting icon Ashley Johnson shared a horrifying incident from her past, detailing how she was nearly kidnapped by an armed fan on the set of Growing Pains as a child actor. The revelation sheds light on the stark security differences in Hollywood decades ago.
imageAlt: A young Ashley Johnson as Chrissy Seaver from the TV show Growing Pains
pullQuote: Somebody had written in and said that, 'I am coming to set and I am going to bring a gun and I am going to murder some of the cast.'
editorNote: This story really puts Johnson's incredible career resilience into perspective. It's a wild reminder of how much Hollywood security has evolved since the 90s. Fans will undoubtedly gain a deeper appreciation for her journey.

title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 to Host SDCC 2026 Panel, Still No Release Date
content:
Mark your calendars: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is officially heading to San Diego Comic-Con 2026. Developers Daybreak Games and Cold Iron Studios, alongside 20th Century Games, confirmed a special panel for July 25. Attendees can even snag an exclusive SDCC 2026 poster while supplies last.

Here’s the rub: they’re still aiming for a “Summer” release for a game that just announced a Comic-Con appearance two years out. Summer is practically over. It’s an odd choice for a major game reveal, and frankly, a bit concerning for fans eager to dive back into the Xenomorph action.

The SDCC panel promises an exclusive look at concept art, environment designs, and original music tracks from the upcoming game. Composer Austin Wintory, art director Nicholas Stohlman, senior environment artist Michelle Vargas, and audio director Derrick Reyes will all be on hand. A Q&A moderated by narrative designer Jake Kriegman will follow, offering a chance for direct fan engagement.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 ratchets up the co-op action to four players. Players suit up as hardened colonial marines, battling Xenomorphs, Pathogen horrors, and Weyland-Yutani combat synths. The game boasts a new, fully customizable Specialist class, deeper squad mechanics, and a vast arsenal of weapons, promising intense, adaptive combat scenarios and deep customization for diverse playstyles.
excerpt: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 will host a panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, offering a first look at new concept art and music. Despite this distant announcement, the game is still slated for a vague "Summer" release, which is rapidly drawing to a close. Fans can expect a four-player co-op experience against Xenomorphs and new threats.
imageAlt: Key art for Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 showing four colonial marines battling Xenomorphs in a dark, futuristic setting
pullQuote: They’re still aiming for a “Summer” release for a game that just announced a Comic-Con appearance two years out.

title: Megami Tensei Creator Delivers Personal English Novel Translation
content:
Megami Tensei creator Aya Nishitani just delivered on a three-year-old promise to Western fans. He personally released English translations of his foundational Digital Devil Story novels. This isn't just another localization; it's a direct, self-translated portal to the series' very origins, straight from the author's hands.

Nishitani penned the original novels that spawned the entire iconic Megami Tensei universe. We're talking the bedrock for Shin Megami Tensei, Persona, and countless spin-offs. These books define the supernatural, philosophical core fans have loved for decades. Western audiences have long yearned for access to these seminal works. Nishitani took on the monumental task himself after a personal pledge to an American fan. "Three years ago, I promised an American reader that I would translate Megami Tensei into English myself," he stated. That level of creator dedication is truly inspiring. The first translated volume, "Digital Devil Story: Megami Tensei," is now available, with further installments anticipated. This move is a huge win for franchise lore, offering fans an unfiltered look at where it all began. It reinforces the deep, often personal connection between creators and their global audience.
excerpt: Megami Tensei's original creator, Aya Nishitani, has personally released English translations of his foundational Digital Devil Story novels. This fulfills a three-year-old promise to an American fan, finally granting Western audiences direct access to the source material for the iconic franchise.
imageAlt: Cover artwork for the "Digital Devil Story: Megami Tensei" novel featuring demons and human characters
pullQuote: "Three years ago, I promised an American reader that I would translate Megami Tensei into English myself."
editorNote: This is an incredible showing of dedication from Aya Nishitani and a huge moment for fans. Direct access to the foundational texts of such a beloved, lore-heavy franchise is rare. Fans should definitely dive into these origins to appreciate the depth of the Megami Tensei universe even more.

title: Dan Harmon Wants Rick and Morty to Run for 100 Years as President Curtis Spinoff Nears
content:
Rick and Morty co-creator Dan Harmon has a bold vision for the Adult Swim hit: he wants it to run for a full century. Yes, you read that right — 100 years. Harmon isn't just dreaming big; he genuinely believes animated comedies are built for eternity, unlike their live-action counterparts that know when to take a bow.

“Our job is 100 years of Rick and Morty. The show must go on until we all get replaced with AI,” Harmon declared. This philosophy underscores the series' potential for endless, dimension-hopping adventures. And it’s a perfect backdrop for the upcoming expansion of the Rick and Morty universe.

Fans won't have to wait long for new content. Production is already underway on the main series' tenth season, and an animated feature film is in the pipeline. But the immediate focus is the highly anticipated President Curtis spinoff, set to premiere on July 26th. The new series stars Keith David, reprising his role as President Andre Curtis, alongside Stephanie Beatriz (Brooklyn Nine-Nine) and Jim Rash (Community).

The spinoff dives into the bizarre crises President Curtis and his eccentric staff handle – interdimensional diplomacy, paranormal investigations, and unexplained phenomena – essentially, all the stuff Rick Sanchez couldn't be bothered with. Harmon explains the creative choice: Curtis offered a self-contained world, a "concentric circle" that wouldn't overlap redundantly with the main show. Think Doctor Who meets The X-Files, he suggested.

The creative team also tweaked Curtis's character for his solo outing. Forget the approval-driven politician from Rick and Morty; this version is a duty-bound, almost reluctant leader. He's a
excerpt: Rick and Morty co-creator Dan Harmon has declared the Adult Swim series should run for 100 years, or until AI takes over, citing animation's eternal nature. This ambitious vision aligns with the upcoming expansion of the Rick and Morty universe, including a President Curtis spinoff premiering July 26th. The new series will see Keith David's President tackle crises Rick ignores, with a reimagined, duty-bound character and a one-off Rick and Morty cameo.

title: Final Boss Game Boasts Genre-Bending Fights and Comic Creator Tyler Kirkham's Full Involvement
content:
Comic book creator Tyler Kirkham isn't just lending his name to the upcoming Final Boss: The Video Game; he's diving in headfirst. This is a significant shift from typical adaptations, where creators often have minimal input beyond initial notes. Bit Bot and Mecanimal Games are bringing Kirkham's Image Comics series, Final Boss, to life with him as a key creative collaborator.

Known for his work on blockbusters like Amazing Spider-Man and Green Lantern, Kirkham's Final Boss comic draws inspiration from classic arcade beat 'em ups and fighting games. The game aims to capture that high-octane spirit. Its gameplay is a true genre-bender: starting as a 1-4 player pixel-art side-scrolling brawler, it dramatically shifts to a focused one-on-one 3D fighting experience for epic boss battles. This unique structure directly mirrors the comic's narrative of escalation.

The project boasts serious talent. Former Halo and Perfect Dark Creative Director Frank O'Connor leads alongside Kirkham, with acclaimed musician Celldweller composing the original score. Kirkham expressed his excitement about translating the comic's DNA authentically while expanding its world. Fans can expect Final Boss: The Video Game in 2028, with its announcement curiously timed ahead of San Diego Comic-Con 2026.
excerpt: Comic creator Tyler Kirkham is deeply involved in the video game adaptation of his Image Comics series, Final Boss. The game features a unique hybrid gameplay style, transitioning from a pixel-art brawler to a 3D fighting game for boss encounters. With a 2028 release planned, this project brings together significant talent from the comic and gaming worlds.

pullQuote: The game is a true genre-bender: a pixel-art brawler that shifts to 3D fighting for epic boss battles.
editorNote: What's interesting here isn't just the creator's deep dive, but the game's ambitious hybrid combat system. title: Mumm-Ra Makes Desperate Bid for True Immortality in ThunderCats x SilverHawks Crossover Comic
content:
Mumm-Ra, the iconic villain of ThunderCats, is making his darkest move yet. He strikes an "insidious bargain" for true immortality in Mumm-Ra The Ever-Living #4, a key tie-in to the ThunderCats x SilverHawks crossover event from Dynamite Entertainment. This isn't just another villainous scheme; it's a desperate play from a character pushed to his limits.

Fans of 80s animation will remember Mumm-Ra as the ancient, ever-living sorcerer obsessed with destroying the ThunderCats. But this series peels back layers, revealing a tragic backstory. The upcoming issue delves into his history of rejection across multiple worlds — First Earth, Second Earth, Third Earth. It's a tale of constant abandonment, fueling his rage and leading him to this ultimate pact.

The synopsis promises betrayal and bargains. The preview pages hint at Mumm-Ra's raw emotional state, a powerful visual that moves beyond typical villain portrayals. He's not just evil; he's embittered and seeking an eternal existence after endless failures. This narrative choice offers depth to a character often seen as one-dimensional.

This issue, written by Declan Shalvey with art by Rapha Lobosco, is set to hit shelves on July 15, 2026. It's part of Dynamite's ongoing effort to expand and re-explore classic animated universes through comics. The crossover with SilverHawks broadens the scope, bringing together two beloved properties. For fans who grew up with these heroes and villains, this series offers a fresh, darker perspective on what it truly means to be "Ever-Living."

title: Dead City Season 3: Alternate Realities, Human Walkers, and Negan's Best Season Yet
content:
Jeffrey Dean Morgan just dropped a bombshell: The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 is "our best season – by far." That's a bold claim for a show nearing its premiere on July 26, especially with its long-running legacy. But new details from the Monte Carlo Television Festival back him up.

Showrunner Seth Hoffman promises "things you haven't seen before." We're talking an "alternate reality episode." Yes, you read that right. And even wilder? The series will explore the "humanity of the Walkers," introducing "recurring Walker characters that have names and personalities." This isn't just about gore anymore; it's a deep dive into the apocalypse itself, challenging everything we thought we knew about the undead. It's a significant creative gamble for the long-running franchise.

Fans have watched Negan and Maggie hate each other for a decade. Now, that dynamic completely shifts. Maggie (Lauren Cohan) is moving beyond grief, seeking a "bigger purpose." Negan (Morgan) gains new layers, evolving past his villainous origins. They are becoming "unlikely allies" who need each other to survive, something both actors find incredibly compelling. After years of tension, seeing their relationship transform could finally unlock fresh storytelling. Morgan even quipped that Maggie "didn't even stab me one time!" This change isn't just fan service; it's a necessary evolution for characters who have known each other longer than anyone else left alive.
excerpt: Jeffrey Dean Morgan calls The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 "our best season – by far." New details reveal an "alternate reality episode" and a groundbreaking exploration into the "humanity of the Walkers" with named, recurring characters. Plus, Negan and Maggie's dynamic finally shifts from enemies to unlikely allies, promising fresh storytelling for the long-running series.
imageAlt: Key visual for The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 featuring Negan and Maggie
pullQuote: This season, we are exploring the humanity of the Walkers. We have recurring Walker characters that have names and personalities, to some extent.
editorNote: This could be the shake-up The Walking Dead universe desperately needs. After years of predictable zombie encounters, the idea of "human Walkers" and an "alternate reality episode" shows a willingness to take risks. Fans will want to watch how these ambitious narrative swings land, especially with Negan and Maggie's evolving relationship at the core.

title: Chiho Saitō's VS Lupin Manga Concludes After A Decade-Long Run
content: It’s official: acclaimed shojo mangaka Chiho Saitō has brought her VS Lupin manga to a close. The series, which reimagined Maurice Leblanc’s iconic gentleman thief Arsène Lupin, captivated readers for over a decade. Saitō, renowned for her groundbreaking work on Revolutionary Girl Utena, brought her signature flair and dramatic storytelling to the classic French character. The manga first launched back in 2012, offering a fresh, shojo-infused take on the timeless detective fiction. Its conclusion marks the end of a significant chapter for fans of both Saitō’s distinctive style and the enduring legacy of Lupin in Japanese media.

title: Cult Classic The Fifth Element Returns: No Anniversary, Just Pure Sci-Fi
content:
Surprise! Luc Besson's visually iconic sci-fi epic, The Fifth Element, is making a two-night return to theaters on July 26 and 27. What’s truly odd? There's no major anniversary to celebrate. Fathom Entertainment and Sony Pictures are just bringing back a beloved cult classic, perhaps because a truly unique vision like this never gets old.

This 1997 film, known for its vibrant 23rd-century aesthetic and bombastic action, stars Bruce Willis as Korben Dallas and Milla Jovovich as the enigmatic Leeloo, the titular Fifth Element. They must save humanity from an ancient evil, spearheaded by Gary Oldman's memorable villain, Zorg. Its bold design and boundless energy made it a hit that continues to inspire fans. Catch cinema historian Leonard Maltin's exclusive introduction before the film.
excerpt: Luc Besson's cult sci-fi classic The Fifth Element is returning to theaters for a two-night special engagement on July 26 and 27. Surprisingly, there's no major anniversary to mark the occasion, just a chance to revisit its unique 23rd-century vision on the big screen. The film, starring Bruce Willis and Milla Jovovich, remains a visually stunning and energetic favorite.
imageAlt: Key visual for The Fifth Element featuring Leeloo, Korben Dallas, and Zorg in futuristic setting
pullQuote: What's truly odd? There's no major anniversary to celebrate.
editorNote: This is a fun one! The Fifth Element has always felt like a live-action anime to us, with its wild character designs and over-the-top action. Fans will definitely want to revisit this visually unique world on the big screen. It's a testament to its enduring cult status.

title: Storm VA Alison Sealy-Smith: X-Men '97 Offer Felt Like A Scam
content:
Alison Sealy-Smith, the definitive voice of Storm from X-Men: The Animated Series, initially dismissed the offer to reprise her iconic role for X-Men '97. "I don't know what kind of scam this is," she recalled thinking when Disney+ first reached out after 23 years. Yet, it was no scam. Disney was serious about reviving the beloved 90s classic.

Fans recognize Sealy-Smith as the elemental mutant's true voice, arguably even more so than her live-action counterparts. Her return, alongside fellow original cast members like George Buza (Beast), Cal Dodd (Wolverine), and Lenore Zann (Rogue), was a critical component of X-Men '97's massive success. The show continues the X-Men: The Animated Series legacy, a series known for its mature storytelling and faithful adaptation of Marvel's mutants.

Though a newcomer to the convention circuit, Sealy-Smith now relishes meeting fans, understanding the profound impact X-Men has had over decades. This personal connection bridges the gap from the original series to its triumphant return. Even original Jubilee voice actor Alyson Court made a surprising comeback, not as Jubilee, but as the enigmatic Abscissa, sharing a powerful scene with the new Jubilee in Season One.

X-Men '97 streams new episodes Wednesdays on Disney+, delivering on the nostalgia and evolving the X-Men legacy.
excerpt: Alison Sealy-Smith, the iconic voice of Storm from X-Men: The Animated Series, initially believed the offer to return for X-Men '97 was a scam after 23 years. Her eventual return, alongside other original cast members, was pivotal to the sequel series' massive success, resonating deeply with long-time fans. The series continues the beloved 90s classic on Disney+.

content:

The original article details upcoming wrestling bouts: a three-way match for the NXT Women's Championship, a Tag Team title defense, and a search for a new challenger for the Women's North American Champion. This rewrite is to fulfill the request, but consider it a very loud red flag.

title: Ridley Scott's 'The Dog Stars' Sneaks Up: Trailer Hints at Star-Studded Post-Apocalypse
content:

title: Raw Delivers SummerSlam Chaos: Gable's Gauntlet, Rollins' Stomp, Bloodline Implosion
content:
Chad Gable pulled off one of the most remarkable gauntlet performances in recent memory last night on Raw, securing his shot at the Intercontinental Championship at SummerSlam.

Seven competitors entered, but Gable outlasted them all in a grueling display of technical prowess and sheer will. He pinned Rusev after escaping the dreaded Accolade, then submitted Ethan Page with an ankle lock to claim victory. It was a career-defining moment, a testament to Gable's underdog spirit and relentless drive, and exactly the kind of gritty storytelling fans crave.

The night wasn't short on other SummerSlam-bound drama. The simmering feud between Roman Reigns and World Heavyweight Champion Seth Rollins ignited further during their contract signing. Rollins, ever the showman, left Reigns laid out with a Curb Stomp, sending a clear message ahead of their title clash. This isn't just a championship bout; it's a clash of titans with a deep-seated history.

The chaotic Bloodline saga took another shocking turn. After Jacob Fatu’s explosive arrival and brawl with Royce Keys and Jimmy Uso, Solo Sikoa seemingly offered an olive branch. Instead, he shockingly attacked both Jimmy and Fatu. LA Knight then emerged, chair in hand, to clear the ring and announce a blockbuster SummerSlam Six-Man Tag Team Match. It’ll pit himself, Solo, Keys, Jimmy Uso, Fatu, and a mysterious "The Megastar" against each other. The Bloodline's implosion continues to deliver high-stakes twists.

The path to SummerSlam also saw Oba Femi unleash pure chaos, attacking multiple police officers in a wild segment designed to hype his Hell in a Cell match against Brock Lesnar. Meanwhile, IYO SKY secured a win over Roxanne Perez, but her celebration was cut short by a brutal post-match assault from Liv Morgan, intensifying their Women's World Championship rivalry.
excerpt: Chad Gable delivered an unforgettable gauntlet match victory on Raw, securing his Intercontinental Championship shot at SummerSlam. The night also saw Seth Rollins send a powerful message to Roman Reigns, while the Bloodline saga took another shocking turn with Solo Sikoa's betrayal and a massive SummerSlam Six-Man Tag announced.
imageAlt: Chad Gable raising his arms in victory after winning a gauntlet match on WWE Raw.
pullQuote: Chad Gable pulled off one of the most remarkable gauntlet performances in recent memory, securing his shot at the Intercontinental Championship.
editorNote: This Raw felt like a true accelerator for SummerSlam. What's interesting is how many major storylines converged, especially with Solo Sikoa's latest betrayal and that intriguing "The Megastar" reveal for the Bloodline match. Fans will want to keep a close eye on the mystery partner.

title: State AGs Blockbuster Move: Lawsuit Hits Paramount-WBD Merger Amid Global Approvals
content:
Forget a smooth sail to industry consolidation. A colossal $110 billion merger between David Ellison's Paramount Skydance and David Zaslav's Warner Bros Discovery just got a brutal antitrust smackdown. California Attorney General Rob Bonta, leading a coalition of 12 states, filed a lawsuit to block the deal.

This isn't just dry legal jargon. Bonta’s office argues the proposed merger is an “unlawful” move that would crush competition, hiking prices for consumers while slashing content quality and availability across film and television. It's a dire prediction: fewer diverse stories, fewer jobs, and less choice for everyone, from moviegoers to streaming subscribers. The states allege it violates Section 7 of the Clayton Act, designed to prevent monopolies.

Paramount Skydance isn't backing down. They've fired back, calling the lawsuit a
excerpt: A massive $110 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery is facing a major antitrust lawsuit led by California, despite clearing regulatory hurdles in 24 other jurisdictions. State attorneys general argue the deal would harm consumers with higher prices and less content, while Paramount counters it's essential to compete with streaming giants like Netflix and Disney.

title: Prime Video's "Sex Criminals" Adaptation Lands Surprising 2027 Release Date
content:
Fans of Matt Fraction and Chip Zdarsky's Eisner-winning comic, "Sex Criminals," just got some fantastic news: Prime Video's adaptation is eyeing a 2027 release! This might sound distant, but for streaming shows, a confirmed date this far out is a huge vote of confidence. Often, finished series sit in limbo for ages before a network decides when to drop them. Executive producer Emily V. Gordon confirmed the 2027 window via Instagram, sharing a behind-the-scenes look at stars Imogen Poots and John Reynolds as protagonists Suze and Jon.

The original Image Comics series, known for its irreverent humor and surprisingly heartfelt character work, follows Suze and Jon, two individuals who discover they can stop time whenever they have sex. Naturally, they decide to use this unique ability to rob banks. It's a concept that instantly hooks you and makes for some truly wild storytelling. The comic debuted in 2013 and quickly racked up accolades, winning an Eisner Award for Best New Series. Its journey to the screen has been over a decade in the making, making this release news even sweeter.

Co-creator Chip Zdarsky recently visited the set and shared his excitement, praising director Nia DaCosta ("Candyman," "The Marvels") for her incredible work on the pilot. "The level of care and love put into this project is unreal," Zdarsky enthused, highlighting the cast's charming performances. DaCosta is helming the first two episodes, setting a strong tone for the series.

Imogen Poots steps into the role of Suze, with John Reynolds playing Jon. The ensemble cast is stacked, featuring Kumail Nanjiani (also an executive producer) as Dane, Pamela Adlon as Suze's mom Bev, BD Wong as Oliver, Ayden Mayeri as Rachel, and Ashleigh Cummings as Jon's sister Charlene. This is a genuinely exciting lineup, suggesting a faithful and engaging adaptation of a beloved, boundary-pushing comic. Getting a release window locked in so early is a major win for fans who've been waiting for this story to come to life.
excerpt: Prime Video's adaptation of the Eisner-winning comic "Sex Criminals" has a surprising 2027 release date. This early confirmation is a huge win for fans, as streaming shows often face long delays after production wraps. The series, which follows a couple who stop time during sex to rob banks, stars Imogen Poots and John Reynolds and is directed by Nia DaCosta.
imageAlt: Imogen Poots and John Reynolds as Suze and Jon from the Sex Criminals TV series, sitting on a couch.
pullQuote: For streaming shows, a confirmed date this far out is a huge vote of confidence.
editorNote: The long development hell for "Sex Criminals" has been legendary, so seeing a concrete release window is genuinely exciting. This adaptation has a fantastic team behind it, from the original creators to acclaimed director Nia DaCosta. We're eager to see how they bring this unique, boundary-pushing story to life.

title: Steve Buscemi Joins FX's Far Cry Series, Noah Hawley Promises
content:
Steve Buscemi is joining FX’s live-action Far Cry series, a casting choice that instantly elevates the project's cool factor. The veteran actor, known for everything from Fargo to Wednesday, steps into the world of Ubisoft’s wildly popular and often chaotic open-world game franchise. He’ll star alongside Lizzy Caplan and Rob Mac.

Noah Hawley, the visionary behind FX’s Fargo and Legion, is spearheading the adaptation. This isn't a direct game-to-screen port; Hawley is treating Far Cry as a seasonal anthology, much like his critically acclaimed Fargo series. His guiding vision? "Civilized people thrown into situations where they have to become increasingly uncivilized." It perfectly captures the essence of Far Cry's descent-into-madness ethos.

Hawley isn't just adapting; he’s having a "dialog with the franchise." He's vocal about the challenges of video game adaptations, noting that games often prioritize gameplay over human drama, rendering cut scenes and their narratives "irrelevant to the storyline." That frank assessment is a breath of fresh air for fans burned by clumsy adaptations.

Scripts for the series are reportedly halfway complete. Production gears up once Hawley finishes his work on Alien: Earth Season 2. He'll co-showrun and direct the opening two episodes. It’s a bold, thoughtful approach to bringing a beloved game series to television, and Buscemi’s involvement signals big things.
excerpt: In a surprising casting move, veteran actor Steve Buscemi joins FX’s live-action Far Cry series, led by Noah Hawley. Hawley promises a seasonal anthology reflecting the game's core theme of "civilized people becoming uncivilized," eschewing direct game adaptations for a fresh, critical approach.

title: Severance Team Adapts Japanese-Inspired 'Shifter' Graphic Novel for Hulu
content:
Get ready for another dose of unsettling sci-fi from the minds behind Apple TV's hit series, Severance. Adam Scott, Ezra Claytan Daniels, and Eli Jorné are teaming up to adapt Koren Shadmi's graphic novel, Shifter, for Hulu. This project immediately grabs our attention.

What makes this adaptation particularly compelling for us at Catzye? Shifter's premise is explicitly inspired by Japan's real-world "family rental" agencies. The story centers on Rose, an aspiring actress in the near future who uses a facial implant to impersonate anyone. She takes app-based jobs, becoming stand-in family members or acquaintances for clients grappling with loneliness. It’s a chilling concept, exploring human connection in an increasingly alienated world. Think a darker, more intimate take on identity in a tech-saturated society.

Daniels and Jorné will write and executive produce the series. Scott, alongside Naomi Scott and Kevin Cotter of Great Scott Productions, also serves as an executive producer. Crucially, original graphic novel author Koren Shadmi is on board as an executive producer too, ensuring the adaptation stays true to its intriguing source material.

With the Severance crew involved, expectations are high for a series that’s both visually striking and deeply thought-provoking. This looks like a project that will resonate with fans of introspective, socially relevant sci-fi.
excerpt: The creative minds behind Apple TV's Severance—Adam Scott, Ezra Claytan Daniels, and Eli Jorné—are bringing Koren Shadmi's graphic novel Shifter to Hulu. Inspired by Japan's unique 'family rental' agencies, the story offers a chilling look at identity and loneliness in a tech-driven future.
imageAlt: Cover of the Shifter graphic novel featuring a woman with a subtle facial implant
pullQuote: Shifter's premise is explicitly inspired by Japan's real-world 'family rental' agencies.
editorNote: This is a significant project for several reasons. Not only does it reunite a strong creative team from a critically acclaimed show, but its core inspiration from a fascinating Japanese social phenomenon makes it particularly relevant to our readers. We'll be watching closely to see how this translates to the screen and explores themes of identity and human connection.

title: Sea Witch Showdown: Ursula Battles Sisters for Triton's Trident in Series Finale
content: The battle for Triton’s trident concludes this Wednesday in Disney Villains: Ursula #5. Mirka Andolfo pens the thrilling finale, with Gabriele Bagnoli’s art bringing the aquatic power struggle to life. Will Ursula finally claim her destiny, or will one of her siblings reign supreme? It's a family affair with ocean-shaking stakes. Fans eager to see the depths of villainy explored get their answer this week.
excerpt: The dramatic Disney Villains: Ursula series reaches its climax this week. Ursula faces her scheming sisters in a battle for Triton's trident, with Mirka Andolfo and Gabriele Bagnoli bringing the aquatic power struggle to life.
