title: Infernal Hulk #9 Drags Bruce Banner Into Soul Cages
content:
The Infernal Hulk #9 drops this Wednesday, dragging Bruce Banner into a literal hellscape. Forget just smashing: Banner and Doctor Voodoo are embarking on a perilous 'suicide mission' into the mystical Soul Cages. Their goal? Steal a mysterious weapon, a stark contrast to the widespread destruction Infernal Hulk is wreaking across the globe with his 'Fallen Army.'

The Infernal Hulk himself isn't idle. He's got the Baxter Building in his sights, convinced Reed Richards holds a secret weapon capable of stopping his conquest. Even Carol Danvers, Captain Marvel, finds herself roped into a critical cosmic delivery mission, highlighting the massive scale of this conflict.

Writer Phillip Kennedy Johnson and artist Adam Gorham continue to craft a brutal, psychologically charged run. This series consistently delves into Hulk's darkest identities and Banner's fractured psyche. Fans have embraced its mature themes and visceral action. This issue promises to escalate the stakes even further for a series that’s redefining the Green Goliath. Pick it up this Wednesday.
excerpt: Infernal Hulk #9 promises a twisted journey this Wednesday as Bruce Banner and Doctor Voodoo venture into the mystical Soul Cages on a dangerous mission. Meanwhile, the Infernal Hulk attacks the Baxter Building, setting up a clash with Reed Richards and involving even Captain Marvel in a cosmic delivery. This next installment continues a brutal, psychologically intense run for the Green Goliath.
imageAlt: Cover art for The Infernal Hulk #9, showing Infernal Hulk with glowing eyes and jagged teeth, surrounded by green energy.
pullQuote: Bruce Banner and Doctor Voodoo are embarking on a perilous 'suicide mission' into the mystical Soul Cages.
editorNote: This run of Hulk has been relentlessly dark, exploring a fascinating new facet of Banner's rage. Seeing him team up with Doctor Voodoo for a spiritual heist is a wild direction we're here for. Fans should brace for some serious psychological horror alongside the expected smashing.

title: Hulk Hogan's TNA Meltdown: Dark Side of the Ring Pulls Back the Curtain on Dixie Carter's Chaos
content:
Fans of wrestling's darker corners, brace yourselves. VICE TV's critically acclaimed Dark Side of the Ring is about to dissect one of pro wrestling's most awkward breakups: Hulk Hogan's controversial exit from TNA. The docuseries promises to lay bare not just the "Hulkster's" departure, but also how then-TNA President Dixie Carter allegedly made a bad situation even worse.

Total Nonstop Action Wrestling, or TNA, famously emerged as the rebellious challenger to WWE's monopoly after Vince McMahon absorbed WCW. Founded by Jeff Jarrett, TNA was a beacon of hope for many, known for its high-flying X-Division and distinctive six-sided ring. But behind the scenes, it was a constant battleground of power struggles and financial turmoil. Hogan's arrival, alongside Eric Bischoff, was meant to be a game-changer, but instead, it led to even more internal friction.

The upcoming episode, the third and final part of a three-part deep dive into TNA, spotlights the truly embarrassing way Hogan was written off television. It highlights the questionable creative choices made during that tumultuous period, with Dixie Carter's leadership firmly in the crosshairs. Expect unfiltered insider accounts from wrestling legends and personnel as creators Evan Husney and Jason Eisener pull back the curtain on this messy chapter.

Dark Side of the Ring is renowned for unearthing the most scandalous and tragic stories in wrestling. This season also promises to explore the journeys of legends like Paul Orndorff, Ray Traylor (The Big Boss Man), and the groundbreaking Missy Hyatt, alongside the infamous Necro Butcher vs. Samoa Joe match.
excerpt: VICE TV's Dark Side of the Ring is set to tackle the contentious and embarrassing departure of Hulk Hogan from TNA, shining a spotlight on how then-President Dixie Carter's decisions exacerbated the situation. The acclaimed series promises to peel back the layers on one of wrestling's most awkward breakups, offering insider accounts from those who lived through TNA's chaotic era.
imageAlt: Key art for Dark Side of the Ring episode featuring Hulk Hogan and Dixie Carter from TNA Wrestling
pullQuote: The docuseries promises to lay bare not just the 'Hulkster's' controversial departure, but also how TNA President Dixie Carter allegedly made a bad situation even worse.
editorNote: This episode is a must-watch for any wrestling fan curious about the often-chaotic world behind the scenes, especially during TNA's 'golden' era. Hogan's run in TNA was notoriously divisive, and seeing Dark Side of the Ring tackle it promises unfiltered insight. What's interesting is how directly they're framing Dixie Carter's role in the creative fallout.

title: European Classic Ghost Blitz Heads to North America in 2027
content:
Fans of quick-thinking tabletop games, listen up: the European sensation Ghost Blitz is finally making its North American debut. Maestro Media will publish the beloved classic, designed by Jacques Zeimet, in January 2027. It’s a long-overdue expansion for a game that’s been an immense hit across Europe for over 15 years, yet largely unheralded stateside.

Ghost Blitz is pure, chaotic fun. Players race to grab the correct object from five wooden pieces—a ghost, book, chair, bottle, and mouse—based on a revealed card. It’s a lightning-fast test of observation and reflexes where instinct triumphs over strategy. Correct grabs earn points; mistakes cost dearly. This addictive formula made it a staple in countless European game nights.

Javon Frazier, CEO of Maestro Media, calls it "one of those rare games where instinct beats strategy." He adds, "It has earned its place as a modern classic." This move by Maestro Media is a significant win for North American tabletop enthusiasts eager to experience this proven hit.
excerpt: The beloved European tabletop game Ghost Blitz, designed by Jacques Zeimet, is finally coming to North America in January 2027, courtesy of publisher Maestro Media. Known for its chaotic, quick-thinking gameplay, this marks a significant expansion for a game that has been a hit across Europe for over 15 years.
imageAlt: Box art for the Ghost Blitz board game, featuring a cartoon ghost and game pieces
pullQuote: Ghost Blitz is one of those rare games where instinct beats strategy.
editorNote: This is huge for tabletop fans who've heard whispers of this European gem for years. It's great to see a publisher like Maestro Media recognize its potential for a wider audience. Prepare for some seriously fast-paced, high-stakes fun.

title: Amazon's Mass Effect Series Confirmed: New Story After Original Trilogy, No Shepard
content:
Amazon’s Mass Effect live-action series is forging its own path, diving into a brand-new story set after the original trilogy. That means no Commander Shepard retread — a significant move for the beloved sci-fi RPG franchise. Writer and producer Daniel Casey recently confirmed that work continues, with the writers' room actively crafting this ambitious new vision.

Doug Jung (Mindhunter, Star Trek Beyond) is helming the project as writer, showrunner, and executive producer. Earlier, Michael Gamble of Electronic Arts, a key partner on the series, revealed that the team is closely collaborating with Amazon. The writers room is deep into crafting how this new narrative fits seamlessly into the expansive Mass Effect canon.

The Mass Effect franchise, renowned for its rich lore and player-driven choices, burst onto the gaming scene in 2007 from BioWare and EA. Fans have long dreamed of a faithful adaptation, and Amazon’s commitment to an original, post-Shepard story signals a confident step forward. This isn't just an update; it's a green light for something genuinely new.
excerpt: Amazon’s Mass Effect live-action series is forging its own path, confirmed to tell a brand-new story set after the original trilogy, explicitly moving beyond Commander Shepard’s legendary saga. Writer Daniel Casey recently confirmed active progress on the show, which Doug Jung is helming as showrunner.
imageAlt: Key art for the Mass Effect video game franchise, showing Commander Shepard and squadmates in a spaceship
pullQuote: Instead of rehashing Commander Shepard’s saga, the series will explore a brand-new story set after the original trilogy.
editorNote: This is a smart move by Amazon. Treading new ground allows the series to avoid direct comparisons to the games, offering something fresh for fans while potentially attracting new viewers. What's interesting is how tightly this new narrative will integrate with the existing canon, especially with a new game also on the horizon.

title: War Wolf #7 Throws Thomas Bruin into Paternity Scandal Amidst Alien Apocalypse
content:
This Wednesday, humanity’s last hope faces a devastating alien invasion — and a paternity scandal. Mad Cave Studios, an indie publisher known for its genre-bending comics, drops War Wolf #7. It pushes protagonist Thomas Bruin, known as 'The Bear,' to his absolute limits. Earth is reeling from an assault by the Oorts, an extraterrestrial menace. Yet the planet's biggest distraction isn't the invaders; it's the escalating rumors that Bruin might be the father of the dreaded Oort Worldkiller.

Writer Steve Orlando pens the latest chapter, with art by Marco Perugini and a striking cover from David Talaski. The War Wolf series is known for its gritty sci-fi action and exploring the blurred lines between hero and monster. This issue dives deeper, forcing Bruin to confront his own self-pity. He realizes that in a world on the brink, the truth about his past may not matter as much as his next move.

War Wolf #7 promises to strip Bruin down to basics. He prepares to lead humanity’s final stand across all fronts — from battered city streets to the halls of power. It’s a gripping narrative for fans who love their sci-fi action served with a healthy dose of moral ambiguity and deeply personal stakes. Don’t miss this one.
excerpt: War Wolf #7 drops this week, throwing humanity's last hope, Thomas Bruin, into a scandalous paternity drama. As Oort aliens ravage Earth, rumors swirl that Bruin fathered the mysterious 'Worldkiller.' It's a high-stakes blend of personal crisis and global apocalypse.
imageAlt: Cover art for War Wolf #7 featuring Thomas Bruin, an alien Worldkiller, and a devastated planet Earth.
pullQuote: Rumors swirl about whether he fathered the Oort Worldkiller; believers and doubters battle louder than the invaders themselves.
editorNote: This kind of personal drama amidst galactic stakes is a classic sci-fi trope, but War Wolf seems to lean into it hard. Fans of morally complex heroes and high-octane action will want to check this out. It's a clever twist on the 'reluctant hero' archetype.

title: Dead City Season 3: Walkers Get Personalities and Negan & Maggie Find... Mutual Need?
content:
Get ready for a zombie apocalypse reimagined. The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 is about to shatter expectations, not just with its core duo, but with the very undead themselves. Showrunner Seth Hoffman revealed a game-changing plan: exploring the 'humanity of the Walkers.' Yes, you read that right. Fans can expect recurring walker characters, each with names and burgeoning personalities. It’s a bold, almost revolutionary move for a franchise built on mindless hordes, promising a 'brand new' feel while staying true to its roots.

But the innovations don't stop there. The upcoming season plunges deeper into the fraught, fascinating relationship between Negan (Jeffrey Dean Morgan) and Maggie (Lauren Cohan). After years of bitter enmity and uneasy alliances, their dynamic takes a monumental shift. Morgan declared this 'our best season – by far,' emphasizing a profound change in their bond. Cohan added that Maggie is finally moving beyond grief, driven by a 'bigger purpose' and the stark realization of their mutual dependence for survival.

Morgan humorously pointed out the extent of this shift: 'She didn't even stab me one time!' After a decade of on-screen hate, the two have reached a point where, to survive, they undeniably need each other.

AMC Global Media kicked off promotions for the July 26th premiere with a New York City fan activation, featuring surprise walker appearances. But the true draw here isn't just the marketing; it’s the show’s commitment to evolving its world and characters in genuinely surprising ways.
excerpt: The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 promises to shake up the zombie apocalypse with a surprising twist: recurring walker characters featuring actual personalities. Beyond the undead, the new season dramatically shifts the dynamic between Negan and Maggie, with star Jeffrey Dean Morgan calling it 'our best season – by far.'
imageAlt: Key art for The Walking Dead: Dead City Season 3 featuring Negan and Maggie
pullQuote: This season, we are exploring the humanity of the Walkers. We have recurring Walker characters that have names and personalities.
editorNote: This could be a massive game-changer for The Walking Dead universe, pushing the boundaries of what a zombie story can be. Fans of character-driven narratives will also be thrilled to see the Negan/Maggie dynamic evolve so dramatically. It’s a good sign that this long-running franchise is still willing to take risks.

title: WWE's Survivor Series: WarGames Heads to Houston's Daikin Park, Doubling Down on Stadium Events
content:
WWE just dropped a bombshell, announcing Survivor Series: WarGames will descend upon Houston, Texas, on Saturday, November 28, 2026. This isn't just another show; it's the 40th annual Survivor Series, and it marks a significant return to the city for the first time since 2017.

More notably, the event lands at Daikin Park, home of the Houston Astros, solidifying WWE's aggressive push into major league stadiums for its Premium Live Events. This move follows last year's record-setting Survivor Series at San Diego's Petco Park, signaling a clear strategy: go big or go home. WWE is partnering with Houston First Corporation and the Astros, emphasizing the "world-class event" status and the significant economic impact such shows bring to host cities. Houston boasts a rich history with WWE, having hosted multiple WrestleManias and Royal Rumbles, cementing its status as a premier wrestling destination.

The timing of this announcement feels strategic, especially coming on the heels of AEW's recent "Brawl in the Ballpark" event at Target Field in Minneapolis. While AEW's show was largely an untelevised affair, this latest WWE announcement spotlights the ongoing battle between wrestling's giants for prime real estate and local partnerships. Both promotions clearly see value in tying themselves to major sports venues, elevating their brand presence and fan experience. WWE, with its decades of stadium show experience, is clearly doubling down on this lucrative model.

Tickets for Survivor Series: WarGames go on sale Friday, August 7, with a Club WWE presale kicking off two days earlier. Fans will want to move fast for this one.
excerpt: WWE announced its 40th annual Survivor Series: WarGames will hit Houston's Daikin Park in November 2026, marking a significant return to the city and a continuation of its major league stadium strategy. This strategic move, following last year's Petco Park event, underscores WWE's commitment to large-scale venues and intensifies the competition for prime event locations in the wrestling world.
imageAlt: Key art for WWE Survivor Series: WarGames, featuring the event logo and a view of Daikin Park in Houston.
pullQuote: WWE's strategic push into major league stadiums for Premium Live Events continues, signaling a clear strategy: go big or go home.
editorNote: This announcement clearly demonstrates WWE's aggressive expansion into major sports venues, mirroring a broader trend in professional wrestling. Fans should expect more high-profile stadium events from WWE, and it will be fascinating to watch how AEW responds with its own venue strategy in the coming years.

title: Absolute Batman Animated Series: Original Creators Promise Faithful Expansion
content:
Absolute Batman is heading to animation, and fans can breathe a sigh of relief. Comic writer Scott Snyder is co-showrunning the series, with artist Nick Dragotta also on board as a producer. This isn't just another IP grab; it signals a genuine commitment to the source material.

Warner Bros. Animation and DC Studios announced the adaptation at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, a huge win for fans. Snyder and Dragotta are already deep in preliminary work, crafting the series 'Bible' and planning episode structure. Snyder promises a 'bigger, better, more robust version of the comic on the screen,' aiming for a visual style that brings Dragotta's distinctive art to 'three-dimensional' life.

This won't be a direct panel-for-panel translation, though. Snyder compared the approach to the Wytches adaptation, which expands its comic's story while staying true to its core. The goal is to leverage animation's unique strengths, not just mimic comic panels.

For the uninitiated, Absolute Batman reimagines the Dark Knight entirely. Forget the mansion, the money, the gadgets. This is a working-class hero, facing impossible odds. It’s a mission to prove one person can change the world, even without Bruce Wayne's inherited advantages. 'No manor, no money… all Batman,' Snyder emphasizes. Even DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn has championed the original comic, praising its success. With its original creators at the helm and a clear vision to expand its unique premise, Absolute Batman animation is shaping up to be a faithful, yet fresh, take on the Caped Crusader. This is the kind of creator-led adaptation fans have been waiting for.
excerpt: Absolute Batman is getting an animated series, and the best news? Original comic creators Scott Snyder and Nick Dragotta are leading the charge. Snyder, as co-showrunner, promises a 'bigger, better, more robust' version of the comic, reimagining Batman as a working-class hero.
imageAlt: Key visual for the Absolute Batman animated series, showing a gritty, working-class Batman
pullQuote: This isn't just another IP grab; it signals a genuine commitment to the source material.
editorNote: This creator-led approach is exactly what adaptations need to thrive. Fans will be eager to see how Dragotta's distinctive art style translates to the screen, especially with the promise of a 'three-dimensional' comic come to life. This could set a new bar for how comic book properties are brought to animation.

title: Galaxy's Edge Comic: Hondo Ohnaka Betrays Han and Chewie
content:
Long-time Star Wars fans know that a good betrayal is always just around the corner, and it looks like Han Solo and Chewie are about to get a painful reminder. Marvel Comics' Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge – Echoes of the Empire #4 hits shelves this Wednesday, plunging the iconic duo into a high-stakes double-cross on Batuu.

The issue sees Han and Chewie returning to the Black Spire Outpost, a setting intimately familiar to visitors of Disney's Galaxy's Edge theme park. Their mission? To deliver a crucial relic Princess Leia had escaped with years prior. But trust, as always, is a luxury in the Outer Rim.

Infamous pirate Hondo Ohnaka, a fan-favorite character often seen in Star Wars: The Clone Wars and Rebels, reportedly betrays them. Add the relentless bounty hunter Harkos to the mix, and our heroes are truly in the crosshairs.

Writer Ethan Sacks pens this installment, with art by Jethro Morales and Roi Mercado, promising a dramatic climax to this storyline. It's a direct expansion of the lore that underpins the popular theme park attraction, offering fans a deeper dive into its history.

Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge – Echoes of the Empire #4 arrives July 15th. Grab it to see if Han and Chewie can shoot their way out of this one.
excerpt: Han Solo and Chewie find themselves in deep trouble on Batuu in the latest Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge comic. Infamous pirate Hondo Ohnaka betrays the iconic duo while they're on a crucial mission to deliver a relic for Princess Leia. This issue directly expands the lore of Disney's popular theme park attraction.
imageAlt: Cover art for Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge – Echoes of the Empire #4 featuring Han Solo and Chewbacca
pullQuote: Infamous pirate Hondo Ohnaka, a fan-favorite character, reportedly betrays them.
editorNote: What's interesting here is the continued weaving of comic narratives directly into Disney's theme park lore. Fans visiting Galaxy's Edge will appreciate the deeper context this series provides for Black Spire Outpost. It's a smart way to connect different facets of the Star Wars universe.

title: Knicks Star Jalen Brunson Steps into WWE Ring with Roman Reigns
content:
Hold up, sports fans (and, let's be real, wrestling fanatics)! In a crossover twist nobody saw coming, New York Knicks star Jalen Brunson is stepping into the squared circle, or at least ringside, with WWE's Tribal Chief Roman Reigns. This isn't just a friendly handshake; Brunson is set to join Reigns at WWE Saturday Night's Main Event on July 18, 2026, live from Madison Square Garden.

The announcement hit like a finishing move: Reigns himself extended the invite via social media, and the "King of New York" accepted. This move clearly aims to capitalize on the Knicks' championship buzz – yes, the NBA champions – and inject some much-needed mainstream hype into Saturday Night's Main Event.

But here's the real story behind the spectacle: this particular WWE show isn't enjoying the prime-time spotlight of Raw (Netflix) or SmackDown (USA Network). Instead, it's buried exclusively on Peacock. Ouch. This high-profile crossover feels less like a celebration and more like a desperate power-up for a show struggling to find its footing on a crowded streaming platform.

And speaking of power-ups, remember Danhausen? The very nice, very evil performer whose supposed mystical powers somehow blessed the Knicks' playoff run? Brunson himself admitted, "I was a little skeptical at first, but you have to believe now." Could Danhausen, the purveyor of curses and good omens, make an appearance at MSG? That's the kind of chaotic energy this event desperately needs.

What will Brunson actually do alongside the undisputed World Heavyweight Champion? WWE's press release is vague, teasing "What will Brunson have in store?" Don't expect him to trade his basketball sneakers for wrestling boots and challenge Reigns for the title; the Tribal Chief is already slated to defend against Seth Rollins at SummerSlam. This is about drawing eyes to Peacock, pure and simple.

The blend of championship-level sports and scripted entertainment is a classic move to generate buzz. But for Saturday Night's Main Event, it’s also a stark reminder of its diminished broadcast platform. Will the Knicks' magic, coupled with Roman Reigns' undeniable star power and a dash of Danhausen's mystique, be enough to make this Peacock exclusive a must-watch? Fans will have to tune in on July 18th to find out if this bold crossover delivers a championship-worthy performance or just another promotional stunt.
excerpt: In a surprising crossover, NBA Champion Jalen Brunson will join WWE's Roman Reigns at Saturday Night's Main Event on July 18, 2026, at Madison Square Garden. This high-profile appearance aims to generate buzz for the show, which streams exclusively on Peacock, and possibly leverage the recent "mystical" connection with wrestler Danhausen. It's a clear move to boost a platform struggling for mainstream attention.
imageAlt: Split image of Jalen Brunson in a New York Knicks jersey and Roman Reigns in WWE championship attire
pullQuote: This high-profile crossover feels less like a celebration and more like a desperate power-up for a show struggling to find its footing on a crowded streaming platform.
editorNote: This crossover is a fascinating look at how major brands are leveraging star power to drive engagement on streaming-exclusive content. For fans of surprising collaborations, this is definitely one to watch. What's interesting is how they're pulling in the 'meta' narrative of Danhausen's influence.

title: GameSir's New Xbox Controller Blends '90s Nostalgia With Cutting-Edge Tech
content:
Remember the translucent tech trend that defined the late '90s? GameSir is bringing it back in style with their new T7 Pro W Retro Green wired controller for Xbox and PC. But don't let the nostalgia fool you; this isn't just a throwback design, it's packed with cutting-edge features.

Its standout innovation? Hall Effect sticks and triggers. That means no more infuriating stick drift, a common bane for serious gamers. Precision is paramount here, whether you're nailing complex combos in a fighting game or fine-tuning your aim, thanks to features like two-stage trigger stops.

Comfort and customization are also key. Four integrated rumble motors immerse you deep in the action, while two programmable back buttons offer extra control. A 3.5mm audio jack is a welcome inclusion, essential for many gamers.

This controller keeps it simple and reliable with a wired USB connection, ensuring low-latency input and uninterrupted gameplay without worrying about batteries. GameSir's Nexus software lets you tweak everything, from button mapping and sensitivity to RGB lighting, and save profiles for your favorite titles.

All this retro-futuristic goodness comes in at a budget-friendly $50. It’s a smart move from GameSir, offering a compelling blend of classic aesthetics and modern performance without breaking the bank.

title: A24's Crystal Lake Teaser Reimagines Friday the 13th as '70s Psychological Thriller
content:

The series dives deep into the psyche of Pamela Voorhees, Jason's mother, with Linda Cardellini in the lead role. Forget the traditional slasher formula; Kane calls Crystal Lake a "paranoid '70s thriller" and a "character piece" exploring Pam's unraveling grief after her son, Jason, dies. It's a bold move, stripping away the machete for psychological horror, though Kane promises "rivers of blood" and "ingenious kill sequences" that serve the narrative.

Kane emphasizes the show's roots in the original film's era: the mistrust, women's liberation, and social awakening of the 1970s. This isn't just a backstory; it's a re-examination through a modern, prestige horror lens, a hallmark of A24's work. Cardellini herself took on the "unexplored" role because of its potential, and Kane already calls her "inconceivably brilliant." William Catlett, Devin Kessler, and Callum Vinson (as young Jason Voorhees) also join the cast.

Crystal Lake premieres October 15th. It's set to challenge expectations for the franchise, pushing it into ambitious, character-driven territory that feels right at home with A24's reputation for elevated horror.

title: DC Comics Unleashes "Anti-Price Gouging" Rules on Variant Covers
content:
DC Comics just hit the collector market with a major policy shift. The publisher unveiled new "anti-price gouging" terms for exclusive retailer variant covers, directly targeting the skyrocketing prices and speculative practices that have plagued releases like Absolute Batman. This isn't just a suggestion; it's a bold move to rein in a "pocket industry" built on scarcity and hype.

The new rules are crystal clear. DC explicitly bans retailers from selling variants in blind bags, mystery packs, or similar promotions. This directly impacts operations like Felix Comic Art, which recently advertised $100 blind bags guaranteeing an Absolute Batman foil variant — now a forbidden practice. Beyond that, retailers face strict price caps. They can't charge more than five times the standard cover price for variants, or ten times for rarer foil editions. This means a $6 variant can't exceed $30, and a $10 foil variant is capped at $50. Retailers like Mark Brooks Art Store, known for selling variants at $50-60, are now outside these guidelines.

Unsurprisingly, the collector community is divided. Some praise DC for stepping in, hoping it curbs rampant speculation and makes coveted covers more accessible. However, many argue the policy misses the mark entirely. "If DC forces them to charge significantly less for variants, scalpers will buy them all up," one Reddit user commented. The prevailing sentiment is that DC creates the scarcity with limited print runs, then blames retailers for inflated prices. Critics suggest this move will only empower secondary market speculators, who will simply buy up cheap variants from retailers and flip them for massive profits, untouched by DC's new terms.

This move raises big questions for the entire collectibles market. Will it truly help fans, or just shift the profit from retailers to online resellers? Publishers constantly grapple with controlling market value versus the reality of fan demand and speculation.
excerpt: DC Comics just dropped a major policy change, enacting strict "anti-price gouging" terms for exclusive retailer variant covers. The new rules ban blind bag sales and cap prices, directly aiming at the inflated secondary market for comics like Absolute Batman. Many collectors, however, fear this will only push scalping to online resellers rather than help fans.
imageAlt: Key visual of an Absolute Batman comic book with a prominent variant cover, possibly showing a foil effect.
pullQuote: If DC forces them to charge significantly less for variants, scalpers will buy them all up.
editorNote: This move by DC highlights the ongoing tension between publishers, retailers, and collectors in a speculative market. While the intent might be good, fans will want to watch closely to see if this actually makes coveted variants more accessible or simply fuels the secondary market even further.

title: Moana Tops Box Office, But Underwhelms As Nolan's Odyssey Looms
content:
Moana snagged the top spot at the box office this past weekend, but its victory feels hollow. The animated hit pulled in just $43 million domestically and $95 million worldwide — far below expectations for such a beloved franchise. While audiences who saw it gave it a strong A- CinemaScore, the market is undeniably crowded.

Franchise fatigue appears to be a factor. Moana arrived shortly after Toy Story 5 and Minions & Monsters, stretching family budgets thin. Releasing too close to its predecessors likely didn't help, even with the star power of Dwayne Johnson.

The horror entry Evil Dead Burn faced a different challenge, grossing only $13.7 million — a 44% drop from Evil Dead Rise. This isn't audience fatigue; it's a studio misstep. A confusing marketing campaign and late promotion left potential viewers unsure what to expect.

Now, all eyes turn to Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey. This week brings arguably the year's most anticipated film. Predictions place its opening around $85 million, poised to dominate. However, limited premium format availability might prompt some fans to delay their initial viewing.
excerpt: Moana took the weekend box office crown, yet its $95 million worldwide debut significantly underperformed expectations, signaling potential franchise fatigue. Meanwhile, Evil Dead Burn's weak $13.7 million opening points to poor studio marketing. All eyes now shift to Christopher Nolan's highly anticipated The Odyssey, predicted to open strong despite limited premium format screens.
imageAlt: Key visual for the Moana film showing characters on an ocean wave with the movie title
pullQuote: Moana snagged the top spot at the box office this past weekend, but its victory feels hollow.
editorNote: This isn't just a tough weekend; it's a telling moment for franchise strategy. Studios can't just rely on big names or established IPs anymore. Audiences are discerning, and genuine excitement needs careful cultivation. What's interesting here is how much the industry relies on a few tentpole releases, making these individual outcomes so critical.

title: Nightmare on Elm Street Awakens: But Where's Freddy?
content:
A new Nightmare on Elm Street film is officially in the works, but the biggest mystery isn't the plot – it's whether Freddy Krueger will even be wielding his iconic glove. Paramount's new horror label, Paramount Primal, has secured U.S. rights from the estate of the late Wes Craven to reimagine the original 1984 screenplay.

This is huge news for horror fans. Craven's widow, Iya Labunka, expressed excitement for a new generation to experience the nightmare, a sentiment echoed by Primal's J.D. Lifshitz and Raphael Margules, who called it an "honor beyond words."

Here's where it gets interesting: reports state the new film is "set in the world of A Nightmare on Elm Street, based on the original screenplay." Lifshitz and Margules mentioned "welcoming Freddy home," but that specific phrasing leaves room for interpretation. Could we see a Nightmare film without the Springwood Slasher at the forefront? Recasting Freddy after Robert Englund's legendary run has always been a monumental challenge. Or perhaps we're looking at an animated return for Englund himself? The possibilities are as vast and terrifying as Freddy's dreamscape.

The studio has secured rights to reimagine Wes Craven's original screenplay, sparking speculation about a potential story without the iconic slasher or a new take on his legacy.

title: Sex Criminals TV Series Reveals First Look at Leads, Director Nia DaCosta Praised by Co-Creator
content:
Fans have been waiting over a decade for this, and now we finally have a glimpse! Kumail Nanjiani has shared the first official look at Imogen Poots as Suze and John Reynolds as Jon, the leads in Prime Video's highly anticipated adaptation of Matt Fraction and Chip Zdarsky's Sex Criminals.

But the real kicker came from series co-creator Chip Zdarsky himself. After visiting the set, Zdarsky gushed in his newsletter, singling out director Nia DaCosta for incredible praise. "She's so damned good and wonderful and the show looks absolutely gorgeous," he enthused, highlighting the "unreal" level of care and love poured into the production. This isn't just a quick cash-in; it sounds like a passion project.

The Eisner Award-winning Image Comics series, known for its wildly unique premise—a couple who stop time during sex to rob banks—first launched in 2013. Its decade-plus journey to the small screen has been a saga, with EPs Emily V. Gordon, Kumail Nanjiani, and Tze Chun championing it for years.

Imogen Poots and John Reynolds step into the shoes of the titular time-stopping duo. The ensemble cast also features Nanjiani himself as Dane, Pamela Adlon as Suze's mom Bev, and BD Wong as Oliver. Nia DaCosta, fresh off major projects, is at the helm for the pilot and second episode. Her involvement is a massive vote of confidence for a series with such a distinct, irreverent voice.

Seeing this beloved, boundary-pushing comic finally come to life with such a talented team is a huge win. Zdarsky's enthusiasm, combined with DaCosta's vision, suggests Sex Criminals could truly deliver on its cult classic potential.

title: Global Green Light, US States Say No: Paramount Battles Antitrust Suit Over Warner Bros. Deal
content:
A massive $110 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery faces a surprising, aggressive challenge. Twelve U.S. states are trying to block the deal, even though competition regulators in 24 jurisdictions worldwide have already given it the green light. Paramount isn't holding back, calling the lawsuit "fundamentally flawed" and a "misrepresentation of competition." This isn't just a corporate squabble; it's a fight over the future of media, content creation, and what lands on your screen.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta leads the states, claiming the merger violates antitrust laws. He warns it would lead to "higher prices, lower quality, and less content," hurting everything from movie theaters to everyday viewers. Bonta also expresses concern over fewer opportunities for diverse stories and creative talent, painting a picture of market rigging and a shrinking pool of content.

Paramount Skydance fires back hard. They argue the deal is crucial for a healthy, competitive entertainment landscape. Merging creates a stronger rival to tech and streaming giants like Netflix, Amazon, and Disney, platforms Paramount claims have already hurt the industry. Far from shrinking content, the combined company promises to invest more aggressively in premium content and theatrical releases, aiming for at least 30 high-quality films annually with a guaranteed 45-day theatrical window. More content, more choice, they say.

Crucially, Paramount highlights that global regulators, including the U.S. Department of Justice and Australia's ACCC, found no significant anticompetitive effects. Paramount also emphasizes the deal's benefits for workers, arguing that increased production means more jobs for organized labor. They frame the lawsuit as an attempt to "shield those dominant streaming platforms" and preserve a "failing status quo."

This clash isn't just about two corporate behemoths; it's about the very structure of how entertainment is produced and delivered. Will a larger studio foster more creative output and better compete with monolithic streamers, or will it stifle competition and creativity? Both sides claim to fight for the audience, but their visions are diametrically opposed. The outcome will shape the landscape for creators, distributors, and fans for years to come.
excerpt: A massive $110 billion merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery faces a surprising challenge from 12 US states, despite global regulators giving it the green light. Paramount is vigorously defending the deal, arguing it's essential to compete with streaming giants and will boost content creation and jobs, while states warn of higher prices and less choice for consumers.
imageAlt: Logos for Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery next to each other, representing a potential merger
pullQuote: This isn't just a corporate squabble; it's a fight over the future of media, content creation, and what lands on your screen.
editorNote: This legal battle highlights a core tension in Hollywood: consolidate to compete with tech giants, or fragment to foster diverse voices? For fans, the outcome could determine everything from subscription prices to the sheer volume and variety of films and shows we get. It's a high-stakes poker game, and we'll be watching to see if creators and consumers ultimately benefit.

title: Real Machetes and Retro Tech: How 'They Will Kill You' Forged its Kung Fu Sound
content:
Forget digital bells and whistles. For the kung fu-inspired action-comedy "They Will Kill You," sound designers Jeff Pitts and Duncan McRae went gloriously analog, even using a real, razor-sharp machete to craft its unique sonic punch.

Pitts, the supervising sound editor, revealed he recorded the film's hero machete by hanging a legitimate, sharpened prop on a mic stand. He then proceeded to whack it with his own butcher knife. The result? His butcher knife bent and broke, while the movie prop remained largely unscathed. This dedication to authentic, physical sound capture is a testament to their craft.

Beyond a weapon's durability, Pitts also leaned heavily into vintage gear. He pushed nearly every sound effect through a TASCAM 4-track cassette deck, an old-school piece of equipment that allowed him to manipulate playback speed and create unique Doppler effects. This gave the film's sound a distinct, almost retro texture, fitting its 1970s kung fu cinema homage.

McRae, the rerecording mixer, highlighted the team's relentless pursuit of variety. Each fight sequence in the Kirill Sokolov-directed film was designed to feel different, avoiding any sense of repetition. The final creature fight, for example, required extensive tweaking to achieve the perfect menacing tone, balancing intense music, dialogue, and hard-hitting effects. Earlier brawls often stripped away music entirely, showcasing director Sokolov's willingness to experiment with the soundscape.

Working on "They Will Kill You" reawakened Pitts's appreciation for classic kung fu sound design, a style he now hopes to explore further. That raw, impactful style, often imitated with vocalizations, has a rich legacy, and this film embraced it fully. The film, also starring Zazie Beetz, Tom Felton, and Patricia Arquette, is available on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray, DVD, and streaming on HBO Max.
excerpt: Sound designers Jeff Pitts and Duncan McRae went to extreme lengths for the action-comedy "They Will Kill You," using a real, sharp machete and vintage TASCAM gear to create its distinct sonic palette. The film, an homage to 1970s kung fu, inspired a deeper dive into the genre's unique sound legacy.
imageAlt: A sound engineer working on an audio mixing board, with a classic TASCAM cassette deck in the background.
pullQuote: He recorded the film's hero machete by hanging a legitimate, sharpened prop on a mic stand and whacking it with his own butcher knife.
editorNote: This level of hands-on sound design is truly inspiring, especially when studios are often pushing for faster, more digital workflows. Fans of classic martial arts anime and manga will appreciate the deep cut to kung fu's sonic heritage here. It's a reminder that sometimes, the best tech is the oldest, or just a really good machete.

title: Wonder Woman #35 Reworks Origin Story, Through Steve Trevor's Eyes
content:
Hold onto your lasso, Wonder Woman fans. This week's Wonder Woman #35 drops a new take on Diana's origin story, and it's already raising eyebrows. The twist? It's narrated by Steve Trevor. Yes, you read that right. While he and Trinity race through time to stop the menacing Matriarch, Steve recounts Diana's beginnings, offering a "man who loved her" perspective.

This isn't just a simple flashback. Writer Stephanie Williams and artist Clayton Henry are tackling the "Fates Defied" arc. The preview pages hint at a journey through the River Styx and a glimpse of Diana's mother using a "magic sphere" – essentially an ancient Amazonian surveillance device – to observe the outside world. The core question looms: can Diana's past, seen through Steve's eyes, truly hold the key to saving the future?

For a character as iconic and independent as Wonder Woman, having her origin retold by a male love interest is certainly... a choice. Fans have long celebrated Diana's self-determination and Amazonian roots. Recontextualizing her foundational myth through Steve's lens could offer a fresh, albeit controversial, perspective on her journey. Or it could feel like an odd narrative detour for a hero whose story is fundamentally hers to tell.
excerpt: Wonder Woman #35 is set to revisit Diana's iconic origin story this week, but with a controversial twist: it's narrated entirely by Steve Trevor. While Steve and Trinity race against time, his perspective on Diana's past promises a unique, if potentially divisive, take on the Amazonian hero's foundational myth.
imageAlt: Cover art for Wonder Woman #35, featuring Wonder Woman, Steve Trevor, and Trinity in action
pullQuote: For a character as iconic and independent as Wonder Woman, having her origin retold by a male love interest is certainly... a choice.
editorNote: This narrative choice is bound to spark discussions among longtime Wonder Woman fans. Will Steve Trevor's perspective add fresh layers to Diana's well-established story, or will it overshadow her agency? It's a bold move, and we'll be watching to see how it plays out.

title: Superboy Prime Tears Into Sophie Campbell's Conner Kent in Action Comics #1100
content:
Superboy Prime is back, and he's not just breaking bones — he's breaking the fourth wall to criticize his own writer. Action Comics #1100 delivers a long-awaited, meta showdown between the reality-warping Superboy Prime and Conner Kent, with Prime himself taking issue with how writer Sophie Campbell portrays Conner.

For those needing a refresher, Superboy Prime is a twisted alternate-Earth version of Superman who believes he's the only true hero. He famously caused massive reality changes across the DC multiverse, culminating in him brutally killing Conner Kent during Infinite Crisis. Conner, a clone of Superman and Lex Luthor, was eventually resurrected and uniquely remembers his gruesome death at Prime's hands, along with much of the pre-New 52 continuity. Superboy Prime, ever the comic book fanatic, remembers it all too — because he reads the comics.

Now, in a story written by Sophie Campbell and drawn by Dan Mora, Prime refers to this as the "Sophie Campbell era," sarcastically suggesting they can all "talk about their feelings." But don't expect a therapy session. Instead, Prime rips into Campbell's portrayal of Conner, claiming she wrote him "out of character." It seems even a cosmic-level threat has opinions on social media.

This landmark Action Comics #1100 isn't just a battle; it's a meta-commentary on continuity and character. The issue celebrates 1100 issues of Superman's flagship title with an all-star lineup of talent, including writers Mark Waid, Joshua Williamson, and Dan Slott, alongside artists Skylar Patridge, Ryan Sook, Daniel Sampere, and Lucas Meyer. Catch the drama when it hits shelves on July 22, 2026.
excerpt: Superboy Prime returns in Action Comics #1100 for a meta-showdown with Conner Kent, where Prime not only fights his old foe but also criticizes writer Sophie Campbell's characterization. This long-awaited confrontation reignites their bitter history, punctuated by Superboy Prime's unique, comic-aware perspective. The landmark issue promises a brutal battle and a fascinating commentary on DC continuity.
imageAlt: Cover art for Action Comics #1100 featuring Superboy Prime confronting Conner Kent, with various DC heroes in the background.
pullQuote: Superboy Prime is back, and he's not just breaking bones — he's breaking the fourth wall to criticize his own writer.
editorNote: This kind of meta-narrative is a fascinating trend, especially with a character as unhinged and self-aware as Superboy Prime. Fans will surely debate Prime's 'out of character' critique, which highlights how deeply some readers connect to continuity. It's a bold move for DC, blending a classic rivalry with sharp, self-referential humor.

title: Paramount-WBD Megamerger Halted by Multi-State Antitrust Suit
content:
Hold the phone, Hollywood! The proposed $110 billion merger between entertainment giants Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery just hit a massive snag: a multi-state antitrust lawsuit. California Attorney General Rob Bonta is leading a coalition of 12 states, pushing back hard on the deal.

This isn't just bureaucratic red tape. The lawsuit alleges this mega-merger would drastically lessen competition, leading to higher prices, lower quality, and less overall content for audiences. Think fewer diverse stories making it to screens, whether in theaters or your living room.

Bonta didn't mince words, stating the deal harms "audiences on every sofa and movie theater seat in the U.S." For fans, this is a clear warning shot about market consolidation. Both Paramount and WBD are massive players with deep catalogs, including a growing interest in global content. This legal challenge could reshape the future of how we access our favorite shows and movies.
excerpt: A massive $110 billion proposed merger between Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery is now facing a multi-state antitrust lawsuit. 12 states, led by California, allege the deal would stifle competition, drive up prices, and reduce content diversity for audiences. This legal challenge signals a significant pushback against entertainment industry consolidation.

title: Leaded Gasoline's Wild Ride: SDCC Debut Now, But Standard Release in 2026
content:
Hold on to your hats, comic fans, because Patrick Kindlon and Lorenzo Re's long-awaited Leaded Gasoline is finally making a splash—sort of. After a publishing saga straight out of a horror comic, an exclusive first issue debuts at San Diego Comic-Con in two weeks. The kicker? The standard edition won't hit stores until October 2026. Yes, 2026. The wait, it seems, is far from over.

This isn't Leaded Gasoline's first announcement. Black Mask Studios originally slated it for June 2023, then September 2024, but it never arrived. Earlier this year, Kindlon and Re successfully Kickstarted a hardcover collection. That campaign promised an 'uncensored limited edition' with eight exclusive pages, content not found in future comic or trade releases. That hardcover has yet to ship.

What's the fuss? Leaded Gasoline plunges readers into 1980s South Los Angeles. A brutal killer stalks the streets; a community college professor believes there's a deeper truth behind 'Southside Slayer' inspired murders. Kindlon (Tigress Island) and Re (Firefly) aim for smart, dangerous horror—exactly what Black Mask is known for. Kerbcrawlerghost covers the SDCC exclusive.

It's a bizarre rollout. Collectors face a dilemma: hunt for the SDCC exclusive, await the 2026 standard release, or hope their Kickstarter hardcover ships soon with its unique content.
excerpt: Patrick Kindlon and Lorenzo Re's long-delayed comic, Leaded Gasoline, will debut as an SDCC exclusive first issue, but the standard edition isn't due until October 2026. This complex release follows multiple postponements and a successful Kickstarter campaign promising unique content.
imageAlt: Cover art for Leaded Gasoline issue one by Kerbcrawlerghost, showing dark, gritty horror imagery and the comic's title.
pullQuote: After years of delays, Leaded Gasoline finally gets a San Diego Comic-Con exclusive release, with the standard edition not due until October 2026.
editorNote: This whole situation is a masterclass in how NOT to release a comic, yet it speaks volumes about the creative team's persistence and the audience's anticipation. Fans who backed the Kickstarter will be curious if their unique hardcover ships before the standard comic release in 2026. What a saga!

title: Mike Flanagan's Carrie series blows open Stephen King's lore with 'TK gene' and 'sorority' reveal
content:
Mike Flanagan is about to blow up everything you thought you knew about Carrie White. The horror maestro behind The Haunting of Hill House and Midnight Mass is diving deep into Stephen King’s classic 1974 novel for Prime Video, and his vision for Carrie is far more expansive than previous adaptations. Get ready for a complete reimagining, not just a rehash.

Flanagan revealed his take isn't just a modern update; it's a world-builder. For the first time, the series will explicitly explore King's concept of a "TK gene" and connect Carrie to a larger "sorority of very gifted women." King only hinted at this broader universe, but Flanagan plans to run with it. Every episode after the premiere will even introduce a different woman grappling with her own telekinetic powers, placing Carrie within a much grander tapestry. This is a significant shift, expanding the lore in a way fans have only ever dreamed of.

This new Carrie is also deeply rooted in the "modern teenage experience." Flanagan highlights how King's themes of bullying, empathy, and cruelty are even more relevant today, amplified by technology and social media. Summer Howell plays Carrie White as "wide open," "eager," and "earnest," a stark contrast to past portrayals. Her mother, Margaret (Samantha Sloyan, a Flanagan regular), is framed not as purely punitive, but as fiercely protective, trying to create a "private utopia" to shield her daughter. It’s a completely different dynamic.

Even the iconic prom scene will be reimagined. Flanagan teases a "completely different way" to get there and "completely different" events at the prom itself. He's not just recreating; he's reinventing the entire journey. With Flanagan's proven track record for thoughtful, character-driven horror, this bold new take on Carrie promises to be a gripping, deeply human story about kindness versus cruelty.

The eight-episode series will haunt our screens this fall. Siena Agudong (Resident Evil) joins as Sue Snell, Matthew Lillard (Five Nights at Freddy's) as Principal Grayle, and Amber Midthunder (Legion) as Miss Desjardin. Kate Siegel, Michael Trucco, and Katee Sackhoff are also set for recurring roles, promising a wealth of talent.
excerpt: Mike Flanagan's upcoming "Carrie" series on Prime Video is poised to redefine Stephen King's classic. The adaptation will delve into the "TK gene" and connect Carrie to a larger "sorority of gifted women," a concept only hinted at in the original novel. This expansive vision promises a modern, character-driven reimagining of the horror classic.
imageAlt: Summer Howell as Carrie White, looking eager and curious, set against a subtle, unsettling background.
pullQuote: The series will connect Carrie to a larger "sorority of very gifted women," a concept Stephen King only hinted at.
editorNote: This bold new approach by Mike Flanagan is incredibly exciting. His ability to weave complex characters with genuine scares makes him the perfect choice to expand King's universe. Fans should definitely revisit the original novel to appreciate just how much deeper this adaptation could go.

title: X-Force Implodes: Cable's Plan Fails, Domino Loses Memory in New Issue
content:
Cable's latest high-stakes operation spectacularly backfires, leaving him to pick up the pieces, while Domino faces a sudden, inconvenient case of amnesia. That's the electrifying setup for Inglorious X-Force #7, hitting shelves this July 15th from Marvel Comics. The synopsis teases a potential connection between Cable's "risky move" against the Mutant Liberation Front and Domino's memory loss, suggesting a deeper, more sinister game is afoot.

X-Force has always specialized in the morally ambiguous, the missions no one else will touch. It’s a series built on tough choices and dire consequences. Now, it seems Cable and his team are paying a steep price. Cable, known for his tactical brilliance and time-traveling complications, rarely makes a move without multiple contingencies. For his plan to fall apart so dramatically suggests a truly formidable opponent or an unexpected betrayal.

Meanwhile, Domino’s amnesia is more than just bad luck – it’s a narrative grenade. Her powers rely on probability manipulation, a subtle influence that could be severely hampered by a foggy memory. What vital information has she forgotten? And how does it relate to the Mutant Liberation Front, a group known for its extreme methods in fighting for mutant rights?

Writer Tim Seeley and artist Michael Sta. Maria are at the helm, promising a turbulent ride. Seeley is known for his sharp character work and genre savviness, making him a strong fit for X-Force's blend of action and intrigue. Sta. Maria's dynamic art style should bring the team's predicament and the Adirondack Mountains headquarters to vivid life. R.B. Silva provides the main cover.

This issue is rated T+ and runs 32 pages, priced at $4.99. Brace yourselves, mutant fans. Inglorious X-Force #7 looks set to deliver a hefty dose of tactical failure, mysterious amnesia, and high-stakes mutant action.
excerpt: Cable's latest operation backfires spectacularly, while Domino grapples with a sudden case of amnesia. Inglorious X-Force #7 hits shelves July 15th, promising high-stakes mutant action and a potential connection between these two calamitous events.

Fans should brace themselves for intense fallout from Cable's actions, and Domino's amnesia adds a wild card. We're eager to see how Tim Seeley and Michael Sta. Maria weave these threads together.

title: Slime Season 4 Ends with a Whimper, Not a Bang
content:
That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime Season 4 recently wrapped, and honestly, this arc felt like a masterclass in anticlimax. Fans expected the usual high-stakes action and satisfying kingdom-building beats that make Slime so popular. Instead, what we got was a slow burn that fizzled out.

The pacing dragged significantly. Key plot points, which typically move at a brisk clip in this beloved isekai, seemed stretched thin across too many episodes. While the series often balances political intrigue with monster battles, this season leaned heavily into verbose discussions and less impactful side plots. Where was the epic payoff fans have come to expect from Rimuru's journey?

It's a shame, especially considering the series' strong track record. Slime usually delivers big wins and exciting character development. This season, however, felt largely inconsequential, leaving viewers questioning the overall direction. We hope future seasons rediscover the spark that made us all fall in love with Rimuru and his ever-growing nation.

title: Mike Flanagan's Carrie Series Unleashes a Universe of Telekinetic Women, Reimagines Classic Prom
content:
Mike Flanagan isn't just remaking Stephen King's Carrie; he's blowing the doors open. The celebrated horror maestro revealed his upcoming Amazon MGM series will vastly expand King's lore, exploring a "bigger picture" where Carrie White is just one of many gifted telekinetic women. Even the infamous prom scene will be "completely different." This isn't your mother's Carrie.

While the series is set to have a major presence at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, Flanagan couldn't wait to share details. He told EW he saw an opportunity to modernize King's 1974 classic. Themes of bullying, cruelty, and school violence are more relevant than ever with today's technology, he noted. This series aims to reflect a "modern teenage experience."

Summer H. Howell steps into the iconic role of Carrie White, portrayed as "wide open," "eager," and innately trusting – a stark contrast to previous interpretations. Samantha Sloyan plays her mother, Margaret White, not as purely punitive, but as a fiercely protective woman trying to shield her daughter from a world she doesn't understand. It's a completely different dynamic for the deeply troubled pair.

But the biggest surprise? Flanagan is diving deep into King's original novel's hints about a "TK gene" and Carrie's place in a "sorority of very gifted women." Every episode after the premiere will introduce a new, unique story of another woman, across different times and places, grappling with her own telekinetic abilities. This expands Carrie's isolated trauma into a connected, shared experience.

Fans can expect familiar beats, but twisted. The pivotal prom, a horror touchstone, will unfold in ways entirely new. Flanagan calls it a "wonderfully delicious and irresistible opportunity." With this ambitious vision, Flanagan's Carrie promises to be less a simple adaptation and more an entire universe waiting to unfold.
excerpt: Mike Flanagan's upcoming Carrie series for Amazon MGM Studios isn't just a faithful adaptation; it's a bold reimagining. The show will explore Stephen King's "TK gene" concept, expanding Carrie White's story into a universe of telekinetic women and promising a "completely different" take on the iconic prom scene.
imageAlt: Key visual for Mike Flanagan's Carrie series showing Carrie White with telekinetic powers
pullQuote: The events of that prom are going to be completely different.
editorNote: This is a huge shift from previous adaptations, going far beyond the classic prom. Expanding the lore to a 'sorority' of telekinetic women is an ambitious move that could make this adaptation truly stand out. Fans will want to watch how Flanagan connects Carrie's isolated trauma to a wider, shared experience.

title: The Adventure Zone: Story and Song Delivers Epic 'Balance' Finale
content:
The Adventure Zone: Story and Song, the seventh and final graphic novel adapting the beloved “Balance” arc, just hit shelves, bringing a massive saga to its epic conclusion. This isn't just any finale; it's the culmination of a fan-favorite narrative that has captivated audiences first as a D&D actual-play podcast, then as a bestselling comic series.

The graphic novel run, penned by the McElroy family — Griffin, Clint, Justin, and Travis — with stunning art by Carey Pietsch, has been a runaway success. It's shifted over 1.3 million copies across its previous six volumes, a testament to the series' unique blend of humor, heart, and high stakes. Fans have followed Taako, Merle, and Magnus's journey from humble beginnings to universe-saving heroes.

"Story and Song" throws our heroes into their ultimate confrontation. They face "The Hunger," the cosmic evil threatening to consume all existence. This volume promises an emotionally charged and action-packed finale, delivering on years of build-up. It's a fitting end for a story that has redefined what TTRPG storytelling can achieve, across multiple mediums.

editorNote: This isn't just a comic book release; it's the end of an era for fans who've followed the McElroy family's storytelling since the podcast's early days. The success of this adaptation highlights the power of compelling narrative to transcend mediums. What's next for The Adventure Zone in comics is anyone's guess, but the bar has been set incredibly high.

title: RuneScape Unleashes Massive Player-Owned Housing Update, Redefining Gielinor Life
content:
RuneScape players, the wait is officially over! After years of anticipation, Jagex has finally unleashed the massive Player-Owned Housing (POH) update, completely transforming how you'll live and express yourself in Gielinor. This isn't just a new feature; it's a deep dive into personalization, letting you build a dream home from scratch.

This update dramatically overhauls the Construction skill, making it more dynamic than ever. Imagine: over 650 decorative items, five unique house styles, and complete freedom with room shapes and furniture placement. You can customize everything from flooring to frames, decking out your space with unique achievement, boss, and quest decorations. Showcase your legendary weapons, hard-won Boss Trophies, and rare archaeological finds in dedicated display stations. Your Prestigious Cape finally gets the shrine it deserves!

But it’s not just about solo digs. The new Homestead system allows up to five players to create a shared community, seamlessly visiting each other’s homes and leveraging combined facilities. Control your home's ambiance with a Weather Vane, choose your favorite tunes on a Jukebox, and craft furniture directly. This update is a game-changer, giving players an unprecedented level of control and a true sense of belonging in the long-running MMORPG. It’s a significant evolution for one of gaming’s most iconic worlds.
excerpt: RuneScape finally drops its highly anticipated Player-Owned Housing update, a complete overhaul for Gielinor's adventurers. Players can now build and customize dream homes with unprecedented freedom, showcasing achievements, crafting furniture, and even forming communal Homesteads with friends.
imageAlt: A player-owned house in RuneScape featuring multiple rooms, custom furniture, and display cases for achievements
pullQuote: This update is a game-changer, giving players an unprecedented level of control and a true sense of belonging.
editorNote: This update is a huge win for RuneScape's dedicated community, especially those who crave deeper immersion and creative outlets. It reflects a growing trend in online games to empower players with tools for self-expression and community building, akin to the detailed world-building we love in manga. It also highlights the continued investment in a game that debuted over two decades ago.

title: Fugitive Doctor Unveils New Sonic Screwdriver in Epic 'Circuit Breaker' Crossover
content:
Jo Martin’s enigmatic Fugitive Doctor is making waves, not just with a sleek new sonic screwdriver, but by teaming up with fan-favorite Martha Jones. This isn’t a one-off adventure; it’s all part of the massive multi-platform "Circuit Breaker" event, designed to finally peel back the layers of this mysterious Time Lord.

Fans got their first look at the Fugitive Doctor's updated sonic screwdriver this week. Its design subtly echoes previous incarnations, a neat nod to the Doctor’s storied past. But the real buzz surrounds "Circuit Breaker," an ambitious series of comics, audio dramas, books, and digital experiences that plunges the Fugitive Doctor into a deep dive with UNIT’s Osgood and facing classic foes like the Daleks and Cybermen. Crucially, the September 3rd book, "The Kaleidoscope," written by Jo Martin herself, sees her Doctor joining forces with Martha Jones against The Silence. Now that’s a team-up!

Jo Martin herself expressed her excitement to Radio Times about fleshing out her character. She described the Fugitive Doctor as previously "one-dimensional" on TV, often appearing decisive and no-nonsense. However, "Circuit Breaker" offers "room to breathe" and explore "more nuance," transforming her into a "far more multi-dimensional character." Martin highlighted the opportunity to reveal the Doctor’s vulnerable side, her capacity to question herself, and even her regrets. She sees the Fugitive Doctor's sarcasm and humor as a shield, and this event allows a deeper exploration of her backstory.

This extensive crossover connects the Fugitive Doctor to classic episodes, weaving her into the rich tapestry of Doctor Who lore. It’s a bold move to expand a character who instantly captured imaginations, and a welcome one for those hungry for more from the Doctor's pre-Hartnell past.

title: Black Mask's 'Calexit' Hits SDCC With Timely Take on California Secession, Unveils New Horror Series
content:
Black Mask Studios is once again leaning into the meta-narrative with its San Diego Comic-Con exclusive covers, particularly for its fiercely relevant series Calexit. Creator Matteo Pizzolo and artist Carlos Granda's acclaimed comic, which imagines a California that has seceded from the United States, has a knack for featuring the very convention center it's sold in. It’s a bold, timely commentary that only feels more prescient with each passing year.

For SDCC, fans can grab Calexit: The Battle of Universal City TP, collecting the first three issues as Jamil and Zora fight to liberate Los Angeles from occupying forces. The battle continues with Calexit: Say Goodbye To Hollywood #1 and The Battle of San Onofre, Part Two, completing a two-part story. There’s even a second printing of Say Goodbye To Hollywood #1 featuring a Cineramadome homage cover, a nice nod to cinematic history. Black Mask isn't just selling comics; they're "drop-kicking Fascism" according to Rolling Stone, and Calexit is their signature move.

But the exclusives don't stop with California's fiery independence. Black Mask is also bringing Patrick Kindlon and Lorenzo Re's Leaded Gasoline #1 exclusively to SDCC. Set in 1980s South Los Angeles, this new horror series follows a community college professor who suspects a killer stalking the streets might be more than just a single madman. Inspired by the real-life "Southside Slayer" killings, Leaded Gasoline promises a smart, dangerous take on classic horror, intent on messing with your mind. It’s exactly the kind of gritty, risk-taking storytelling we expect from these creators.

title: Superman’s Childhood Link to Medieval Hero Revealed in Action Comics #1100
content:
Finally! After decades of fan speculation, DC Comics is forging a direct link between Superman and the medieval hero Silent Knight. Action Comics #1100, set for San Diego Comic-Con 2026, will reveal a surprising connection.

Sir Brian Kent, the Silent Knight, first appeared in 1955. This 6th-century hero was long whispered to be a potential ancestor to Superman's adoptive father, Jonathan Kent. The new story, penned by Mark Waid, offers a fresh twist. Clark Kent, as a child, played a video game called Silent Knight 3000, even picking up some rudimentary sword skills from it. A minor detail? Perhaps, but it firmly plants the character into Clark's backstory.

This landmark Action Comics #1100 celebrates the 1950s era of DC. It also features a roster of top talent, including Joshua Williamson, Sophie Campbell, Dan Slott, Daniel Sampere, and Dan Mora, honoring Superman’s incredible legacy. This subtle nod to Silent Knight could be just the beginning of a deeper dive into the Kent family tree. We're watching.

title: Sam Neill's Passing Leaves Peaky Blinders Team "Devastated"
content:
Sam Neill, the legendary actor whose work shaped pop culture for five decades, has passed away at 78. His sudden death has left the team behind the acclaimed series Peaky Blinders "devastated." Neill's family confirmed his passing on Monday, July 13th, noting it was unexpected but that he remained cancer-free.

The Peaky Blinders production released a poignant statement. They called Neill's portrayal of Inspector Chester Campbell "one for the ages." For the show's first two seasons, Neill embodied Campbell, a ruthlessly intense antagonist tasked with cleaning up Birmingham's organized crime. He was despicable, manipulative, yet also charismatic and entertaining – a truly complex villain.

"Sam was one of the key forces that got Peaky Blinders off to a running start, for which we will be forever grateful," the team shared, adding their love and thoughts were with his family. Neill's impact on the series, particularly in establishing its gritty tone and high stakes, was undeniable. His work as Campbell set a formidable benchmark for the show's future antagonists.

The team behind Peaky Blinders expressed their devastation, calling his iconic portrayal of Inspector Chester Campbell "one for the ages." Neill's unexpected death was confirmed by his family.

title: New Series "The World is Dancing" Dives into Ancient Noh Theater
content:
Get ready for a deep dive into classical Japan. A new series, "The World is Dancing," is on the horizon, promising to fictionalize the extraordinary life of Zeami. For those unfamiliar, Zeami Motokiyo isn't just any historical figure; he's the legendary performer and playwright who essentially shaped Noh, Japan's oldest performing art.

Noh theater is a cornerstone of Japanese culture. It's a sophisticated dramatic art, blending music, dance, and poetry with iconic masks and stylized movements. Often considered Japan's oldest continuous theatrical form, Noh offers a stark contrast to the historical settings typically explored in manga and anime. This focus on Zeami and his revolutionary impact on such an ancient art form makes "The World is Dancing" a truly surprising and ambitious project.

This isn't your average historical romp. Catzye is always looking for stories that push boundaries. "The World is Dancing" promises a unique exploration of art, power, and legacy within a pivotal, yet often overlooked, period of Japanese history. As scholars like Marcille Donato underscore, the story of Noh is deeply interwoven with the nation's cultural identity. Fans hungry for a truly distinct historical drama or a fresh take on traditional Japanese arts should definitely mark this one down.
excerpt: "The World is Dancing," a new series, is set to explore the life of Zeami Motokiyo, the foundational figure of Noh theater. This project promises a unique dive into Japan's oldest performing art, offering a distinct historical drama rarely seen in manga and anime. It's a bold departure that could captivate fans of traditional Japanese culture.
imageAlt: Illustration of Zeami Motokiyo, a legendary Noh performer, possibly from a key visual for The World is Dancing.
pullQuote: This focus on Zeami and his revolutionary impact on such an ancient art form makes "The World is Dancing" a truly surprising and ambitious project.

title: Bryan Batt Stars as Cross-Dressing J. Edgar Hoover in Surprisingly Bold Musical
content:
Forget Broadway. Forget the West End. Harry Shearer and Tom Leopold (The Simpsons, Spinal Tap) just premiered their ambitious J. Edgar Hoover musical in a London pub theater. Yes, that J. Edgar Hoover – founder of the FBI. Yes, a full-scale musical about the notoriously closeted, power-hungry director. And yes, "Mad Men" alum Bryan Batt plays him... often in drag.

This isn't a small-scale production. It's a large-cast show with big numbers, somehow squeezed above a pub. Despite opening night jitters and last-minute understudies, the cast didn't miss a beat.

The narrative unfolds in a deathbed flashback, charting Hoover's ruthless rise to power. It delves into his complex relationship with "lifetime assistant" and lover Clyde, exploring the hypocrisy of a man who exploited others' secrets while fiercely guarding his own. Musically, it’s a masterclass in satire. Think classic Big American Musical belters à la "Guys and Dolls" meets the modern bite of "The Book of Mormon."

Batt is magnificent as Hoover. Cruel, cowardly, and Machiavellian, he's a narcissist portrayed with all too human frailty. Batt fully commits, whether in a suit or, more memorably, in gowns, heels, and blonde curls. It's a role Batt, known for playing a closeted character in "Mad Men," clearly relishes, adding a knowing wink for those familiar with his past work.

Hugo Bolton shines as Clyde, Hoover's long-suffering lover and employee. He's camp, fey, and arguably the show's emotional anchor, bearing the weight of Hoover's abuses with surprising resilience and depth. Lucy O'Byrne delivers a standout performance as Maisie, Hoover’s secretary, with a "Cabaret"-esque moment that shifts the entire dynamic. A highlight is a brilliant quartet of Presidents – including Roosevelt, JFK, and Johnson – reflecting on their uneasy relationships with Hoover and his kompromat. It's funny, silly, and pitch-perfect.

The show masterfully satirizes musical theater's tendency to soften villains, yet it becomes a genuinely heartfelt production in its own right. It's a political pantomime, daring to claim it tells the story of 20th-century America better than even "Hamilton."

"Here Comes J. Edgar! A Comedy Musical" runs at London's King's Head Theatre until August 16th. Don't miss this bizarre, brilliant theatrical gamble.
excerpt: Harry Shearer and Tom Leopold (The Simpsons, Spinal Tap) have unleashed "Here Comes J. Edgar!" – a full-scale musical about FBI founder J. Edgar Hoover – not on Broadway, but above a London pub. "Mad Men" alum Bryan Batt delivers a fearless performance as Hoover, frequently in drag, in this satirical yet heartfelt political pantomime.
imageAlt: Bryan Batt as J. Edgar Hoover in a flowing gown, heels, and blonde wig, performing on stage.
pullQuote: It's a political pantomime, daring to claim it tells the story of 20th-century America better than even "Hamilton."
editorNote: This show sounds like a wild ride, and the concept alone is pure genius. Fans of creators taking big swings with historical figures, much like "Oshi no Ko" or "Frieren" recontextualizing fantasy, will want to keep an eye on this. The sheer audacity of it, especially with Bryan Batt in the lead, is exciting.

title: Kizuguchi to Houtai Anime Sets Far-Off 2027 Premiere
content: Brace for a long wait: NANAI Umihoshi's Kizuguchi to Houtai (Wound and Bandage) manga is getting a TV anime, but it won't hit screens until January 2027. That's a significant lead time for an announcement! The series will air on ABC TV and TV Asahi's late-night ANiMAZiNG block, known for its diverse programming. Director Miyuki Ishida, who previously worked as an assistant director for Danjo no Yuujou wa Seiritsu suru? (Iya, Shinai!!), is at the helm. Susumu Yamakawa, known for his series composition on Gokushufudou, will handle the script. An official website and a teaser visual are already out.
excerpt: Get ready for a long wait: the TV anime adaptation of NANAI Umihoshi's Kizuguchi to Houtai (Wound and Bandage) manga is slated for a January 2027 premiere. Director Miyuki Ishida and scriptwriter Susumu Yamakawa are on board, with the series airing on the ANiMAZiNG block.
imageAlt: Teaser visual for the Kizuguchi to Houtai anime, showing characters from the manga
pullQuote: It won't hit screens until January 2027. That's a significant lead time!
editorNote: This long lead time is certainly unusual for an anime announcement. It could mean the production committee is taking extra care, or it might just be a very early heads-up. Fans will want to keep an eye on this one, especially with Susumu Yamakawa's involvement after Gokushufudou.
